items.title: Optimizing circular economy efficiency: an analysis of third-party recovery service providers in capacity-constrained systems
items.abstract: Purpose The rise in environmental degradation demands a shift from linear to circular economy practices. The study aims to develop a circular economy model that integrates it with third-party recovery service providers (3PRSPs) to tackle real-world capacity constraints to improve the performance of the circular supply chain. Design/methodology/approach A multi-objective circular economy model is formulated based on (1) product-mix profitability maximization, (2) environmental deterioration minimization, and (3) non-recoverable product reduction. Two scenario analyses are conducted to analyze the impact of a centralized and decentralized circular economy network. The model is solved using neutrosophic optimization to account for uncertain product return rate and demand. The methodology is also compared with the epsilon-constraint method and interactive multi-objective fuzzy programming, highlighting the superior ability of neutrosophic optimization to handle higher-order uncertainty. Sensitivity analysis is performed by changing the selling price of new and recovered products to assess the financial viability of the model. Findings Scenario B with a centralized circular economy network yields higher profitability due to greater reliance on third-party recovery and reduced fixed costs. Scenario A, featuring a decentralized circular economy network, reduces environmental impact due to localized recovery and shorter logistical distances. Non-recoverable products remain the same in both network designs, underscoring the inefficiency in raw material quality and product design. Sensitivity analysis also indicates that profitability is highly sensitive to the new product pricing strategy. In addition, neutrosophic optimization enhances the robustness of circular economy network design under uncertain conditions. Originality/value The study provides a robust decision-making framework for the integration of the circular economy network with 3PRSPs under capacity constraints.

items.title: Campos territoriales en transición: investigación situada, gobernanza territorial y construcción colectiva del conocimiento
items.abstract: Problem statement: Territorial scholarship analyzes power relations, multiple territorialities, materialities, governance, and transformations; however, an analytical space remains for understanding configurations in which these dimensions are reconfigured interdependently and disputes extend to the conditions through which territory is produced and governed. Objective: To formulate and delimit the concept of territorial fields in transition and examine its implications for territorial governance and collective knowledge-building. Methodology: The article develops a reflexive systematization of a situated research trajectory, organized around six fields of problematization and analyzed through the reconstruction of research problems, findings, conceptual frictions, and processes of situated translation. Results: The comparison identifies reconfigurations of positions, rules, scales, forms of knowledge, materialities, and authority, with different intensities across the fields examined. Conclusions: Territorial fields in transition are proposed as relational, materially situated, multiscalar, and temporally open configurations. Transition is understood as contingent and non-teleological; governance participates in the production of territorial order, while collective knowledge-building constitutes an epistemological and political dimension of that process.

items.title: Circular Urban Design in Colombia: Territorial Innovation Beyond Policies
items.abstract: Design-based, entrepreneurial, and community-led practices remain underexplored drivers of circularity in Colombian cities.While national circular economy strategies position the country as a regional pioneer, they largely prioritise industrial-scale systems and overlook spatial, social, and informal dimensions of circularity.This article examines three cases that illustrate how circular urban design operates in practice: design-driven reuse entrepreneurship in Barranquilla, community-based material circularity in informal settlements in Medellín, and the adaptive reuse of obsolete shopping malls.Together, these cases demonstrate how architecture can function both as a design practice and as a spatial resource for circular transformation.The study argues that integrating locally embedded design approaches, small-scale actors, and community practices can expand existing circular economy frameworks.By linking spatial transformation, material reuse, and social organisation, circular urban design emerges as a form of territorial innovation capable of supporting more inclusive and place-based transitions.

items.title: HOUSEHOLD E-WASTE MANAGEMENT AND CIRCULAR ECONOMY PATHWAYS IN KERALA WITH FOCUS ON POLICY AWARENESS AND DISPOSAL BEHAVIOUR
items.abstract: Electronic waste (e-waste) is posing an increasing challenge to environmental sustainability and human health in India, especially among the digitalizing states such as Kerala. This study examines the household electronic waste generation, disposal, concerns, policy awareness, and opportunities of circular economy through surveying 150 households in January 2026.Results reveal moderate levels of generation (mean ~3.2 discarded items per household in two years; 83% generated less than 20 kg in one year), very high concerns related to health hazards (M = 4.47/5) and environmental contamination (M = 4.34/5), along with dependence on informal scrap dealers (48–60%) despite a low level of confidence in the safety of informal recycling (M = 2.09/5).Awareness about the Haritha Karma Sena regular e-waste collection system was quite high (93%), as well as about the Waste Free Kerala target (78–91%), but knowledge of Extended Producer Responsibility was relatively low (~47%). Only 34–36% participated in 2025 special drives. HKS had an effectiveness rating (M = 4.20/5), meaning it partially incorporated the use of e-waste in the state’s guidelines. Households were keen on better incentives (68-72%), better drives (52-55%), and local recycling sites (65-70%) to encourage a move towards formal systems and promote repairs/repurposing. Informality prevalence, lack of EPR knowledge, and need for incentive-based and localized strategies emerged from this research. Some suggestions include improvement in EPR education, drive organization, incentive programs, and development of formal district-based recycling centers for sustainable e-waste management in Kerala.

items.title: SUSTAINABILITY, TERRITORY, AND CIRCULAR ECONOMY IN THE GREEN HYDROGEN VALUE CHAIN: CHALLENGES AND PROSPECTS FOR THE ENERGY TRANSITION IN BRAZIL
authors: Ana Verucia Leitão da Silva Vasconcelos
items.abstract: A transição energética contemporânea tem impulsionado a busca por alternativas capazes de reduzir a dependência de fontes fósseis e ampliar a participação de recursos renováveis nos sistemas energéticos. Nesse contexto, o hidrogênio verde destaca-se como uma alternativa associada à descarbonização, à diversificação energética e à integração de diferentes atividades produtivas, embora sua consolidação no Brasil esteja relacionada a aspectos de sustentabilidade, organização territorial, infraestrutura e economia circular. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar os desafios e as perspectivas da cadeia do hidrogênio verde e suas contribuições para a transição energética no Brasil. A pesquisa caracteriza-se como qualitativa, desenvolvida por meio de revisão bibliográfica, com base em dissertações, artigos científicos publicados em periódicos e livros, obtidos em repositórios acadêmicos e institucionais, periódicos científicos e plataformas editoriais. A abordagem adotada permitiu articular e interpretar as dimensões da sustentabilidade, do território e da economia circular no contexto da cadeia do hidrogênio verde. Os resultados evidenciaram que a cadeia do hidrogênio verde no Brasil apresenta desafios relacionados à sustentabilidade, à infraestrutura, à organização territorial e à integração circular dos recursos. Constatou-se que sua expansão depende da articulação entre fontes renováveis, infraestrutura energética e logística, planejamento territorial e estratégias de reaproveitamento de recursos. Conclui-se que a integração dessas dimensões pode contribuir para a diversificação dos sistemas energéticos e para o avanço da transição energética brasileira.

items.title: Gastronomy as a catalyst for the circular economy in tourism: a multi-case analysis of UNESCO Creative Cities in Brazil
items.abstract: A economia circular (EC), aplicada aos sistemas alimentares, posiciona a gastronomia como um vetor estratégico. No turismo, essa abordagem valoriza produtos locais, reduz desperdícios e mitiga emissões de carbono. Nesse contexto, o artigo tem como objetivo analisar de que forma os princípios da EC podem ser integrados aos sistemas alimentares no contexto do turismo gastronômico, visando à promoção do turismo regenerativo por meio da valorização da cultura alimentar, dos produtos locais e da redução do desperdício. A pesquisa adotou a metassíntese como procedimento metodológico, caracterizada como um estudo qualitativo voltado à análise e à interpretação integradas de achados provenientes de pesquisas qualitativas sobre um tema comum. Alinhada ao conhecimento contemporâneo sobre EC, sistemas alimentares e turismo sustentável, a pesquisa também contemplou a análise das Cidades Criativas da Gastronomia da UNESCO no Brasil: Belém, Florianópolis, Belo Horizonte e Paraty. Os resultados indicam que a gastronomia é um caminho para a transição rumo a sistemas alimentares circulares, ao fortalecer circuitos curtos de comercialização, estimular a agricultura familiar e agroecológica, valorizar a sociobiodiversidade e fomentar práticas de prevenção e reaproveitamento de resíduos alimentares. Apesar dos desafios relacionados à governança, à infraestrutura e à capacitação profissional, as cidades analisadas demonstram elevado potencial transformador, funcionando como laboratórios vivos de inovação territorial. Conclui-se que a consolidação de sistemas alimentares circulares no turismo depende da articulação entre políticas públicas integradas, da cooperação entre produtores, chefs e gestores de destinos e do reconhecimento da gastronomia como elemento central para o desenvolvimento sustentável e de baixo carbono.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Waste Generation Patterns and Circular Economy Potential in Two Coastal Protected Areas of the Yucatán Peninsula
items.abstract: Inadequate waste disposal in ecologically sensitive reserves threatens biodiversity and water quality, which highlights the urgent need for localized waste management strategies. This study provides a comparative assessment of municipal solid waste generation, its composition, and circular economy potential within two coastal protected areas of the Yucatán Peninsula, such as Isla Arena in Campeche and San Crisanto in Yucatán. Testing the hypothesis that local economic practices dictate waste trajectories, the research integrated a systematic 6-to-7-day household waste characterization study with community surveys, utilizing non-parametric statistical methods. Marked differences were identified between the two communities, with San Crisanto exhibiting a notably higher per capita waste generation rate compared to Isla Arena (0.98 versus 0.25 kg/day). Distinct compositional profiles also emerged for each site, characterized by a predominance of food waste in San Crisanto and a greater prevalence of non-recoverable materials in Isla Arena. The findings underscore the context dependency of solid waste challenges in protected marine–terrestrial interfaces, demonstrating that effective circular economy interventions must reject generic paradigms in favor of strategies calibrated to localized dominance profiles.

items.title: BioExergoEconomics: A Unified Thermodynamic–Environmental Framework Integrating Exergy Analysis, Circular Economy, Life Cycle Assessment and Biological Resource Recovery
items.abstract: The integration of thermodynamic efficiency, environmental mitigation, and circular resource recovery remains a fundamental challenge in the sustainability assessment of agro-industrial systems. Conventional methodologies—such as Exergoeconomics, Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), and Circular Economy (CE) indicators—typically operate in methodological isolation, limiting their ability to quantify trade-offs between energy-intensive biological recovery and environmental mitigation. To address this gap, this study proposes BioExergoEconomics, a novel unified framework that structurally integrates physical exergy analysis, Exergoeconomic cost allocation, carbon and water footprints, and biological resource recovery into a single F-P-R-I-B functional model. The principal contribution is the formulation of the BioExergoEconomics Index (BEC Index), a dimensionless metric that uniquely synthesizes exergy efficiency, circular resource recovery, biological recovery, carbon mitigation, water conservation, and economic performance. The framework is validated through a comparative case study of beef production (1 kg functional unit). Although biological processing increases electricity demand by 47.8%, this localized energy investment reduces upstream agricultural burdens, resulting in a 17.6% net reduction in energy and exergy demand, a 99.4% reduction in freshwater footprint, and a 51.1% decrease in carbon emissions. With a BEC Index of 0.55, the framework demonstrates that electrical exergy investments in biological nodes can drive systemic sustainability.

items.title: ЦИРКУЛЯРНА ВІДБУДОВА ТЕРИТОРІАЛЬНИХ ГРОМАД: ВЕРИФІКОВАНІ ПРАКТИКИ ТА ПРАКТИЧНИЙ ІНСТРУМЕНТАРІЙ МУНІЦИПАЛЬНОГО УПРАВЛІННЯ
items.abstract: The article substantiates the theoretical and applied principles of circular reconstruction of territorial communities of Ukraine in the conditions of large-scale war destruction, significant needs for infrastructure restoration and the need to transition from a linear resource model to the principles of a circular economy. The purpose of the study is to systematize verified practices of circular reconstruction in Ukraine, identify management lessons based on them and form practical tools suitable for direct use by local governments. The emphasis is on the need to transform destruction waste from a problematic component of post-war reconstruction into a resource for reuse, production of building materials and formation of local closed resource cycles. Five verified Ukrainian practices of circular reconstruction for 2022–2026 are systematized: recycling of destroyed building waste in Hostomel with the participation of Neo-Eco; GreenMix pilot project for recycling construction waste in the Kyiv region; resource-efficient restoration of the water supply system of Mykolaiv; implementation of a mechanical-biological complex for processing solid household waste in Lviv; formation of an intermunicipal platform for processing demolition waste in the Mykolaiv region. It has been established that the effectiveness of circular reconstruction depends not only on the amount of funding and availability of technologies, but also on the institutional capacity of territorial communities, the quality of project management, intermunicipal interaction, involvement of local business and the ability to ensure technology transfer. Based on the generalization of practical experience, a matrix for selecting circular instruments was developed based on the ratio of the expected effect and the complexity of implementation. The instruments are systematized into four groups: “quick wins”, “strategic projects”, “background steps” and “considered decisions”. The feasibility of starting the circula

items.title: Mechanisms for Building and Measuring Territorial Resilience: An Integrated Approach
items.venue: Journal of Urban Planning and Development
items.abstract: This article explores the foundations, mechanisms, and evaluation methods of territorial resilience in the context of disaster management. It highlights the importance of a systemic and multidimensional approach, integrating social, economic, environmental, and political factors. Key resilience-building processes include risk identification, preparedness, response, and postdisaster recovery. To assess resilience, both quantitative indicators and participatory methods are considered essential, offering complementary insights. This study underscores the need for integrated strategies and robust measurement tools to enhance territorial capacity to anticipate, absorb, adapt to, and recover from disasters, while guiding informed and sustainable decision-making.

items.title: СОВЕРШЕНСТВОВАНИЕ ОБНАРУЖЕНИЯ ПОЖАРА В КОРПУСЕ КРУГЛОСУТОЧНОГО ПРЕБЫВАНИЯ НА ОСНОВЕ АДРЕСНОЙ ЛОКАЛИЗАЦИИ И ПРОВЕРКИ ПРОЕКТНЫХ РЕШЕНИЙ
items.abstract: рассмотрены проектные решения по совершенствованию обнаружения пожара в здании комплекса «Вожатый» Международного детского центра «Артек». Требуют уточнения фактическая конфигурация системы пожарной сигнализации и защита мансардных и иных помещений. Предложен подход, объединяющий адресную идентификацию места события, выбор извещателей с учётом условий эксплуатации, проверку их размещения по расчётному сценарию и испытания цепи передачи сигнала до запуска оповещения. Адресность облегчает локализацию тревоги и контроль неисправностей, её влияние на время обнаружения следует подтверждать расчётами и испытаниями.

items.title: Acontecimientos traumáticos severos en la industria mexicana de la construcción: pertinencia normativa y factores territoriales
authors: Scott Michel Martin Da Gama Darby
items.abstract: This article analyzes the presence of severe traumatic events (STE) in the Mexican construction industry in accordance with NOM‑035‑STPS‑2018, integrating the perspective of Sustainable Development Goal 8 (SDG‑8) and the national regulatory framework. It examines the influence of nearby urban and non‑urban territories as factors associated with the violent component of STE reported by workers, following the methodology suggested by the NOM. Findings provide partial evidence suggesting that exposure to external threads to the workplace may increase the likelihood of violent STE. It is concluded that future updates to NOM‑035‑STPS‑2018 should clarify the definition of “hazards surrounding the workplace” to strengthen its relevance in high‑risk industries.

items.title: CONSTRUÇÃO DE UMA CIDADANIA TERRITORIAL PARTICIPATIVA: A IMPLEMENTAÇÃO DO “PROJETO NÓS PROPOMOS” EM TIMOR-LESTE
items.abstract: This article analyses the implementation of the "We propose! Citizenship and Innovation in Geographic Education" in a 12th grade Geography class at the Centro de Aprendizagem e Formação Escolar - CAFE, Suai, municipality of Cova Lima, Timor-Leste, 2025. The initiative aimed to promote geographic education and active citizenship, articulating school knowledge with local territorial challenges. The project involved 27 students and four teachers who developed six research projects on local territorial issues, culminating in the submission of projects in the form of powerpoint, poster and photography and participation in the National Congress of the We Propose Project! carried out by the Institute of Geography and Spatial Planning (IGOT), University of Lisbon, on May 8, 2025. The methodology was based on Project-based learning s and problem-based learning, encoyraging territorial observation, data collection and formulation of Community intervention proposals. The results highlight the potential of school Geography in promoting active territorial citizenship and in articulating knowledge with social transformation.

items.title: Unsettling the "non-indigenous:" Mestizo identity constructions and territorial conflicts
items.abstract: This article complicates the dominant narratives of territorial conflicts between indigenous communities and mestizo campesinos in Nicaragua's Bosawas Biosphere Reserve. I suggest that the framing of these conflicts as "interethnic" obscures how class and space shape the multiple, intersectional identities and experiences of mestizo campesinos and justifies their exclusion. Furthermore, the interethnic narrative hampers the distinction between "mestizo" campesinos and "mestizo" elites who facilitate the colonization of indigenous territories through policies prioritizing extractivism and large-scale agriculture that compromise indigenous territorial security and rural lives. In this way, dominant narratives enable violence against both mestizo campesinos and indigenous communities. The article contributes to political-ecological debates on the construction and materiality of seemingly unmarked mestizo identities, which have often remained unexplored in the literature.

items.title: Transformer-based Monte Carlo Localization in Construction Meshes
items.abstract: To be able to perform inspection or digitization tasks, mobile robots on construction sites must be able to localize themselves reliably with respect to a global reference frame that is shared with a building map. Similar room layouts and low-texture surfaces pose a challenge for existing LiDAR- and vision-based localization methods. We approach this problem with a LiDAR-based global relocalization system that estimates the robot's pose relative to a building mesh and combines a PointNet++ encoder with a place recognition decoder, whose outputs serve as a learned observation model within a Monte Carlo Localization (MCL) framework. The pipeline is trained exclusively on synthetic LiDAR scans obtained by simulating the robot's sensors inside the building mesh. Our approach is robust in ambiguous environments due to an uncertainty-aware decoder that scales positional likelihoods and a resampling strategy that injects model hypotheses into the particle set, enabling recovery from potential particle depletion. Evaluations on real-world datasets show that our method outperforms both diffusion-based and ScanContext++ baselines while maintaining fast inference (18 ms per call), demonstrating the practicality of synthetic-data training for mesh-referenced global localization in construction robotics.

items.title: RSM and ANN-driven optimization of Reactive Blue 221 biosorption by inactive Aspergillus niger: Mass transfer mechanisms, pareto analysis, and a circular economy approach
Offsite construction for sustainable building delivery: benefits, challenges and future directions
items.abstract: The construction industry faces increasing pressure to mitigate its global carbon footprint, reduce resource consumption, and minimize landfilled material waste. Offsite construction (OSC) has emerged as an industrialized paradigm capable of restructuring traditional project delivery. This paper presents a critical literature review of 19 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2020 and 2026. The objective is to synthesize the environmental benefits, assess the circular economy potential, and identify the supply chain and digital challenges of offsite building delivery. Results demonstrate that modular and industrialized building systems achieve substantial waste reductions, reaching up to 83.2% in weight and up to 78.8% on average across analyzed building projects. Furthermore, comparative life cycle assessments (LCAs) indicate greenhouse gas (GHG) reductions of approximately 8% under typical logistics configurations, with transport thresholds identified around 120km. Incorporating circular principles, such as Design for Disassembly (DfD), can further reduce global warming potential by up to 63% compared to linear offsite options. However, digital integration remains fragmented, with limited deployment of automated digital twins or artificial intelligence (AI). Moreover, widespread adoption is hindered by high upfront capital costs, design-stage constraints, and logistics complexities. We conclude that offsite construction represents an effective sustainable delivery pathway when combined with circular design frameworks, optimized localized supply chains, and integrated digital workflows.

items.title: Spatial Associations Between the Neighborhood Built Environment and Mental Health: Evidence from Tehran
items.abstract: Built environments influence mental health, yet evidence on how different dimensions of urban form relate to specific mental health outcomes remains mixed, particularly in high-density cities. This study examined these relationships in Tehran, Iran, while accounting for spatial dependence and exploring spatial heterogeneity. Using secondary neighborhood-level data from 356 neighborhoods, five mental health outcomes—anxiety, depression, social dysfunction, somatic symptoms, and overall psychological distress—were analyzed in relation to the built environment. Ordinary Least Squares (OLS), Spatial Durbin Models (SDM), and Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR) were employed to assess global associations, spatial spillover effects, and localized spatial variation. The findings indicate that residential density emerged as the built-environment characteristic most consistently associated with poorer mental health, whereas population density showed no significant direct association with any mental health outcome. Access to daily services were associated with lower somatic symptoms and social dysfunction. Anxiety and depression were explained mainly by neighborhood socio-demographic characteristics, particularly unemployment and neighborhood age structure. Spatial spillover effects were identified only for social dysfunction, while exploratory GWR analyses indicated that neighborhood–mental health associations were predominantly global across Tehran, with only modest evidence of localized spatial variation. These findings demonstrate that different dimensions of urban density have distinct implications for mental health and that different mental health outcomes respond to different neighborhood characteristics. Overall, the results suggest that improving the quality of high-density residential environments, alongside addressing neighborhood socioeconomic inequalities, may be more effective than focusing on urban density alone when promoting mental health in high-density

items.title: Spatial Differentiation and Built-Environment Correlates of Street-Block Vitality in Baoding, China
items.abstract: The spatial differentiation of street-block vitality and its built-environment correlates provide an empirical basis for implementing refined street-block governance in the context of the renewal of existing urban areas. Based on the human–environment relationship theory, this study constructs an analytical framework of “built environment condition–street-block vitality response” and establishes a built environment indicator system based on a five-dimensional (5D) framework encompassing density, diversity, design, destination accessibility, and distance to transit. Empirically, street-block vitality is measured by the block-level average heat value derived from Baidu Huiyan data, representing the relative intensity of population activity within each street block. By integrating objective data—such as point-of-interest (POI) data and road networks—with residents’ subjective perceptions, this study employs spatial autocorrelation analysis, hot spot analysis, and multiscale geographically weighted regression (MGWR) models to identify the spatial patterns of street-block vitality in Baoding during the observation week of 8–14 April 2024 and their local associations with built environment factors. Model performance was evaluated through model comparison, sensitivity analysis, and spatial holdout validation. The results indicated that street-block vitality exhibited significant spatial clustering. High–high clusters were primarily distributed in urban development zones and their adjacent areas in the central-eastern, northeastern, and southwestern parts of the city, whereas low–low clusters were mainly concentrated in ecological protection and ecological control zones in the western, northwestern, and northern parts of the city. The density of scenic facilities (Den_sce), facility-density principal component (PC_FAC), road network density (Den_road), and distance to the nearest public transit stop (Dist_transit) generally showed a positive association with street-block vi

items.title: El espacio Atlántico/Caribe guatemalteco: una construcción histórica y territorial liberal 1871-1959
items.venue: Cuadernos Inter c a mbio sobre Centroamérica y el Caribe
items.abstract: The central motivation of this essay lies in explaining the way in which the representation of the Caribbean territory of Guatemala was constructed since 1871. This orientation entails questioning the way in which the official denominated this space, which implies inquiring about the discursive, ideological and politician to name it "Atlantic". This refers to reviewing the trends in urban settlement movements and the construction of communication routes since colonial times. Underlying the thesis that the aforementioned denomination obeys a certainty on the part of liberal intellectuals to denominate the Caribbean space in the aforementioned way, considering that the waters bathe it constitute a common space with Western Europe, a civilizing paradigm. The reproduction of this appreciation takes place with the persistence of an exclusive discourse that led to the assumption of the region as a "window" towards Europe, ignoring the immediate context.

items.title: Spatons: Spatiotonally Localized Building Blocks for Efficient XR Predistortion
items.abstract: We present Spatons, a family of compositional, spatially localized neural operators for computationally efficient XR (extended reality) predistortion and distortion compensation. XR displays (AR, VR, and MR) suffer from spatial (e.g., geometric) and tonal (e.g., colour) distortions. Frames can be pre-distorted so that the projected image looks as intended. Distortions vary with manufacturing tolerances and projection systems, motivating programmable compensation. Untethered, battery-operated XR systems also require low energy and latency. A Spaton is a hybrid patch-to-pixel block combining tiny Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) with fixed-function interpolation. Using Spatons, we build programmable, computationally efficient pipelines for varied distortion scenarios. On the full spatiotonal Scenario 5, Sequential-5' matches CompenNet++ in SSIM (0.944 vs. 0.944) and closely matches its PSNR (27.5 vs. 27.7 dB), with substantially lower complexity. We demonstrate a flexible Spaton solution with 6 times fewer FLOPs and 106 times fewer parameters than CompenNet++, and 4-10 times fewer memory transfers than UNet++. We characterize software implementations and analytical hardware estimates, including optimizations across target XR platforms. The distortions considered are drawn mostly from see-through, near-eye displays, where the spatial light path governs local intensity and spectral response. This early systems-level exploration uses closed-form differentiable distortions and one real projector-camera capture set for training and evaluation, rather than through-the-optics measurements. Testing on a wider range of real XR devices remains future work. Chromatic dispersion (color fringes) remains the main artifact where Spatons trail monolithic baselines.

items.title: State Territorialisation Without Urbanisation: Governing Rural China Under ‘Rural Revitalisation’
items.abstract: Amid the global dynamics of planetary urbanisation, urbanisation has been the frontier of a state territorialisation process of enhancing territorial control and spatial governance. However, recent state strategies in China, exemplified by Rural Revitalisation, reflect a renewed political focus on rural society within state‐driven spatial governance. This study argues that this shift produces a distinctive form of ‘territorialisation without urbanisation’, where the state consolidates control by governing in place—embedding its authority within rural space without converting it into urban jurisdictions. It does so through both spatially bounded and relationally reorienting mechanisms. Beyond traditional territorial urbanisation approaches such as territorial regulation and administrative upscaling, the state further reconfigures state‐society and state‐market relations via grassroots party‐building and fiscal mobilisation. The study illustrates these techniques based on the governance transformation of a village in southwestern China.

items.title: Digital Entrepreneurship and Territorial Bricolage: The Mechanisms Underlying the Construction of a Smart Territory in Dakhla-Oued Eddahab
items.venue: Revue Internationale des Sciences de Gestion
items.abstract: In peripheral territories with still limited digital resources, the emergence of innovative entrepreneurial practices raises questions about the concrete mechanisms through which digital technology contributes to building a smart territory. This is the case of the Dakhla-Oued Eddahab region, engaged in a digital transformation dynamic driven by national strategies and the Morocco Digital 2030 vision, yet where entrepreneurs must navigate significant territorial constraints. This research aims to understand how entrepreneurs mobilize territorial bricolage to turn these constraints into levers for building a smart territory in Dakhla-Oued Eddahab. The study adopts an interpretivist qualitative stance based on a single case study. Twenty semi-structured interviews were conducted with stakeholders of the regional ecosystem and analyzed through a reflexive thematic analysis assisted by Nvivo12, following an abductive approach. The findings show that the contribution of digital entrepreneurship to smart territory construction rests on the interaction between digital infrastructure, territorial governance, entrepreneurial ecosystem dynamics, and entrepreneurs' adaptive capabilities. They further reveal an emerging mechanism, territorial digital entrepreneurial bricolage, through which entrepreneurs creatively mobilize locally available resources to overcome structural constraints. This mechanism enriches the theoretical model and opens avenues for other comparable peripheral territories.

items.title: Construction Path for Dual-Use Public Infrastructure within the Territorial Space Planning System
items.venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
items.abstract: In the context of advancing urban resilience and modernizing the national governance system, dual-use public infrastructure has emerged as a pivotal spatial carrier for coordinating urban development and security. However, the implementation of the dual-use concept at the planning level faces systemic challenges, including the lack of top-level design, disconnections in transmission mechanisms, and barriers to cross-departmental coordination. This study reviews the conceptual evolution and policy trajectory of dual-use public infrastructure, and explores the jurisprudential logic and integration challenges concerning its alignment with the five-level, three-category territorial space planning system. The study reveals that the development of dual-use infrastructure is by no means a mere stacking of individual projects; rather, it represents a profound transformation of the logic underpinning territorial space governance. Through a comparative case study of three typical cities (i.e., Beijing, Chengdu, and Xi'an), the study identifies four core bottlenecks: jurisprudential conflicts in planning, ineffective indicator transmission, spatial misallocation, and incomplete standards and specifications. Drawing upon the system theory, planning integration theory, collaborative governance theory, and whole-life cycle management theory, this study constructs a closed-loop embedding framework consisting of strategic leadership, spatial constraints, facility coordination, and practical implementation. Accordingly, a systematic embedding pathway is proposed, encompassing four dimensions: strengthening top-level design guidance, optimizing the planning compilation system, reconstructing a collaborative governance framework, and refining laws and standards. This research aims to translate dual-use requirements from policy discourse into statutory planning control requirements, providing theoretical support and strategic references for achieving dual-use coordination and enhancing

items.title: From Skills Gaps to Energy Resilience: Building a Territorialized Solar Workforce Ecosystem in Indonesia
items.abstract: Indonesia’s electricity plan for 2025–2034 projects 69.5 GW of additional generation capacity, including 17.1 GW of solar power, while government estimates associate the plan with 348,057 solar-related job opportunities. These projections make workforce capability a material implementation issue: renewable infrastructure requires technicians, engineers, safety specialists, project managers and locally available operations-and-maintenance personnel. Yet headline job estimates do not reveal whether workers are available in the required occupations, locations or project phases. This article examines how workforce development can be linked to the resilience of solar infrastructure in an archipelagic state. It uses a focused qualitative documentary analysis, official Indonesian planning and employment documents, and international institutional evidence, interpreted through energy security, capacity development and energy justice perspectives. The analysis identifies four interlocking governance gaps: incomplete skills intelligence; weak alignment between training, certification and project demand; uneven territorial distribution of operational capability; and limited feedback from infrastructure performance into workforce planning. The article proposes a territorialized solar workforce resilience framework in which workforce data, competency standards, work-based learning, local maintenance capacity and critical-infrastructure performance are planned together. The framework is a theory-building contribution, not an estimate of causal effects. Before journal submission, its propositions require validation through comparative project-level fieldwork and verified occupational data.

items.title: How patriotic discourse informs territorial politics: discursive construction of love, path, and leadership
items.abstract: This research challenges the conventional distinction between patriotism and nationalism and conceptualises patriotism as an open-ended discursive resource whose meaning and effects emerge through situated analysis. Using China’s official discourse on the Taiwan question as a case study, we examine how patriotic discourse informs territorial politics, demonstrating the value of situated analysis. Drawing on Ahmed’s notion of nation as an effect of collective movement and applying the DHA, we analyse how China invokes patriotism in its framing of the Taiwan question. The analysis of the 41 presidential remarks reveals how patriotism is invoked and mobilised in state discourse through historical narratives, continuity framing, metaphorical conceptualisation, and argumentation strategies. Moreover, by distilling patterns from explicit elements in China’s official discourse, we conceptualise patriotism as a regulated trajectory comprising ‘orientation’, ‘prescribed path’, and ‘guiding force’ for examining how meanings of patriotism are channelled in territorial politics.

items.title: Autonomous paths for the localisation of foreign public buildings in the modern Jiangnan region, China, based on a mixed method
items.abstract: Between 1840 and 1949, the Jiangnan region, represented by Jiangsu Province and Shanghai, experienced the proliferation of foreign-influenced architecture. The eclectic integration of architectural forms produced a postcolonial paradox, increasingly blurring the distinction between Western colonial influence and indigenous cultural subjectivity. This paper examines modern foreign public buildings in Jiangnan through a mixed method, integrating literature analysis, entropy weight method, and case study analysis to investigate autonomous paths for the localisation of foreign architecture. Firstly, through a literature analysis of 179 representative publications over the past two decades, nine architectural elements that constitute building form were identified. Secondly, using 83 representative foreign public buildings in the Jiangnan region as samples, the entropy weight method was employed to measure weights, thereby revealing three potential autonomous paths in the localisation process of architecture. Thirdly, case study analysis was conducted by selecting typical building samples for interpretative analysis, verifying the three autonomous localisation paths and elucidating their underlying selection logic in foreign public buildings in the modern Jiangnan region. The findings indicate that: (1) a stable localisation characterised by high weight and low entropy is manifested in the design of building’s main material structure, plan shape contour, plan spatial form, and building roof material structure, reflecting an autonomous path of cultural integration; (2) an adaptive localisation characterised by medium weight and medium entropy is manifested in facade shape contour, reflecting an autonomous path of precise adjustment; (3) a differentiated localisation characterised by low weight and high entropy is manifested in plan proportion, facade proportion, building door and window material structure, and facade decorative pattern, reflecting an autonomous path of fle

items.title: Construction of Discrete Computational Schemes for Studying Tribosystems with Localized Contact Interaction
items.abstract: Purpose. Improving the resistance of electric locomotives to wheelset slipping has always been one of the most pressing challenges in railway transport. Wheelset slipping leads to increased wear on wheel tires, raises the risk of traction motor failure, and creates hazardous operating conditions. The aim of this study is to analyze potential circuit configurations for traction motor excitation control systems that enhance slip resistance and enable the generation of a constant-power traction characteristic. Methodology. The methodological basis of the study comprises the general principles of systems analysis, decision-making theory, mathematical analysis, the modeling of electromechanical systems, theoretical mechanics, and electric traction theory. The study employed established methods for analyzing electromechanical processes in electric traction machines, specifically methods for calculating the magnetic characteristics of electric motors and the traction characteristics of electric locomotives. Findings. The research has identified the most rational circuit configurations for the excitation winding power supply system of traction motors, ensuring high resistance to wheel slip and establishing the locomotive’s limiting constant-power tractive characteristic. Principles for regulating traction motor magnetic flux have been proposed to achieve this constant-power tractive characteristic. A comparative analysis of proposed circuit designs for traction motor excitation systems was conducted. It was determined that the most advantageous option is a separately excited system utilizing a multi-turn excitation winding with low control current; however, this approach necessitates the modification of the traction motors. Conversely, a mixed excitation system with a single winding requires the least modification to the traction motors, but it relies on a low-voltage, high-current power source, which is not energy-efficient. items.title: Characterization of localized circularly polarized THz electric fields using MAPbI3 thin films
items.abstract: Circularly polarized (CP) terahertz (THz) fields are promising for controlling angular momentum in solids. While resonator structures can be used to enhance THz electric fields, a highly localized enhancement makes it difficult to accurately characterize the amplitude and polarization of the local near-field maximum using thick electro-optic crystals. We demonstrate a local probing method based on a band edge modulation in methylammonium lead iodide (MAPbI3) perovskite thin films. The THz-induced transmittance change, ΔT, in the near-infrared (as well as the reflectance change, ΔR) can be used to determine the near-field amplitude, while the degree of the modulation of ΔT (or ΔR) due to the oscillating THz electric-field vector yields the ellipticity ε. The extracted ellipticity is close to the ideal value (within ±0.05) for ε > 0.4. A comparison with finite-difference time-domain simulations shows that this method can be used to characterize the amplitude and ellipticity of the enhanced CP field in the gap of a crosshair resonator with good accuracy. The simulations also reproduce the experimentally observed long-lived near-field waveform well and indicate that the observed difference between the theoretical and experimental ε mainly arises from a probe spot that is slightly displaced from the gap center by about 1 μm. Since this resonator structure has an enhancement factor of 11.8 ± 0.3 and a high preservation of circularity, the combination of this resonator with the proposed probing method should be useful for studies using strong THz fields.

items.title: Construction of Discrete Computational Schemes for Studying Tribosystems with Localized Contact Interaction
items.abstract: Purpose. Assessment of the reliability and operability of elements of contact pairs of friction nodes of transport systems requires finding the parameters of the stress-strain state that arises in structural elements during their operation. Solving this class of problems of mechanics using exclusively analytical methods is not possible due to the arbitrariness of the shape of parts, spatial variation of mechanical properties, localization of load distribution and fastening conditions. In this regard, the purpose of the work is to create computer-oriented calculation and computational schemes for establishing the influence of the force component of contact interaction on the functioning of tribological pairs of railway transport. Methodology. A comprehensive analysis of modern computational schemes for solving contact problems for solid deformable bodies is carried out, the advantages and disadvantages of each of them for engineering and scientific calculations, as well as for practical implementation in the form of program code for both simple calculations and complex mathematical modeling systems, are shown. Based on the selected penalty method, an algorithm for studying a two-dimensional contact problem for the “wheel-rail” system is proposed. Calculations were carried out based on the author’s algorithm, which was based on the finite element method, the Fenics framework and its implementation in the Python language. The MatPlotLib package was used for further processing and displaying the obtained stress parameters. Findings. The calculations performed established that the results of solving the problem of contacting bodies depend on the boundary and contact conditions, their mechanical properties, as well as on the parameters of the penalty functions in the selected solution search method. items.title: Obsolete Airports as Regenerative Urban Fields: Agroproductive Land, Circular Construction, and Intergenerational Housing in Lisbon
items.abstract: Airports occupy extensive, specialized territories within metropolitan regions. Where relocation is planned, their future becomes a consequential urban question: how can land organized around aviation support new relationships between dwelling, production and ecological recovery? This paper explores the regenerative urban field as a spatial response, examining Lisbon’s Humberto Delgado Airport as a case of prospective infrastructural obsolescence. Existing post-airfield research has advanced landscape and redevelopment approaches, while the integration of productive land, intergenerational housing and circular construction across scales remains less explored. Two complementary design projects are reanalysed through six analytical layers inferred retrospectively from the completed work. Together, they articulate compact urban blocks and inhabited agricultural clusters within a shared territorial scenario, connecting housing and community spaces with cultivation, material choices and proposed water networks. At building scale, an A1–A3 comparison of selected documented materials under a common inventory boundary indicates approximately 31% lower embodied carbon for the proposed strategy than for the conventional reference. The study contributes an exploratory analytical framework for investigating these relationships across scales. It positions prospective airport transformation as an architectural opportunity to organize habitation, productive landscapes and resource systems together, before redevelopment choices become fixed.

Radius of the innermost stable circular orbit of black-holes with localized Astrophysical Dark Matter halo
items.abstract: We investigate the geodesic structure of a static, spherically symmetric black-hole in the background of a localized Astrophysical Dark Matter (ADM)-halo. The halo is modeled by a core-radius ($r_0$), regularized density profile that vanishes at the event horizon and exponential factor ensures the finite total halo mass. We solved the Einstein field equations numerically with equation of state with $p=wρ$ for stiff matter $w=1$ scenario. By analyzing the effective potential and its first and second derivatives, we evaluated the characteristic radius of the time-like innermost stable circular orbit ($r_{\text{ISCO}}$) of massive particle in the vicinity of hairy black-hole. Our numerical analysis is consistent with the recently proposed theoretical upper bound $r_{\text{ISCO}} \le 6$ normalized to unit mass black-hole. We showed that the ADM-halo shifts $r_{\text{ISCO}}$ inward with respect to the Schwarzschild (bald) scenario and the shifts are larger for larger halo core-radius. In particular our numerical finding enumerate $r_{\text{ISCO}}$ are approximately $5.97$, $5.61$, $5.53$ for $r_0=2.0,10.0,20.0$ respectively. We believe that our analysis with ADM-halo model shed light on probing black-hole hair through high-energy astrophysical observables.

items.title: Territorial geopolitics
items.abstract: This chapter discusses the role of boundaries and borders in geopolitics. It begins by defining boundaries, borders, borderlands, and frontiers. These features are identified as a form of territoriality, or the political construction of territory. The process of boundary formation is described as involving the politics of establishment, demarcation, and control. The process of state formation is described as the most important form of territorial geopolitics. Various forms of boundary conflicts are described through the abstract country of Hypothetica. The process of forming peaceful boundaries and the establishment of borderlands is discussed. The case studies of Israel–Palestine and the Korean peninsula are presented as examples. The intersection of geopolitical flows and political boundaries is discussed and exemplified through the case of the European Union and refugees. The territoriality of the sea is introduced, using the example of disputes over island sovereignty in the South China Sea.

items.title: Building Information Modeling in Civil Engineering: Methods, Applications, and Perspectives for Rural Constructions
items.abstract: Building Information Modeling (BIM) can contribute to the design of rural civil engineering structures beyond geometric design by relating building elements to productive activities and environmental constraints. This narrative review brings together BIM, Geographic Information Systems (GISs), farm management, process simulation, and Digital Twin literature to assess their relevance to agricultural buildings. A conceptual Unified Modeling Language (UML) diagram relates building- and performance assessment-related entities and attributes. Software environments are described in relation to their principal design or coordination functions and potential rural applications. A previously published solar-barn dryer study is discussed as an example of linking a parametric BIM representation with reduced-order airflow-network simulation. The synthesis identifies three principal requirements: representing production processes within building information structures; connecting building-scale data to farm and territorial information; and distinguishing offline design simulation from sensor-informed operational Digital Twins. Key research needs concern interoperable agricultural information models, context-dependent implementation costs, and validation against observations from functioning facilities.

items.title: A Localized RAG-LLM System for Safety Compliance Question–Answering in Working-At-Heights Construction
items.abstract: With the advancement of building digitalization and safety management, Working-at-Heights presents challenges due to its complex scenarios and dispersed regulations, making it difficult for on-site personnel to quickly and accurately query and assess compliance. While general-purpose large language models possess text capabilities, they lack professional knowledge adaptation, are not updated in a timely manner, and provide answers without sufficient evidence, thus failing to directly meet the safety and compliance requirements of Working-at-Heights. This paper deploys a localized retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) system based on RAGFlow and Docker. Addressing the safety consultation needs of Working-at-Heights, it transforms regulations and standards into a vector knowledge base. The system integrates keyword and semantic retrieval for precise positioning and aims to reduce hallucinations through source tracing and prompt constraints. Simultaneously, it connects to online retrieval to supplement the latest regulations, achieving a dual-track question–answering (Q&A) mechanism of “local priority, online supplementation.” A typical scenario test set of 100 questions was constructed to evaluate three system configurations across multiple dimensions, including accuracy, traceability, timeliness, and latency. The results show that faithfulness scores increased from 0.45 for the pure large model to 0.91 for local RAG and 0.97 for full-functionality integration, while context recall improved from 0.78 to 0.93 between the latter two configurations. However, response latency also increased from 2.1 s to 4.5 s and 6.8 s, respectively. These findings indicate that local RAG provides more reliable and traceable responses to basic compliance inquiries, whereas full-functionality integration offers superior performance in dynamic information supplementation and handling of unsafe requests. Overall, the integrated approach demonstrates potential for supporting on-site safety co

items.title: Standardized semantic enrichment of OpenBIM for machine-readable pre-demolition audits
items.abstract: The transition to a circular construction sector requires reliable, machine-readable material data from existing buildings. Although reality-capture and emerging scan-to-BIM workflows increasingly support geometric modeling of existing buildings, pre-demolition audits still rely largely on manual interpretation and static reports that downstream tools cannot automatically process. The remaining obstacle is semantic. This paper presents WASTEie2IFC, a web-based framework that addresses this gap by writing audit outputs against the openly published bSDD WASTEie dictionary. The resulting IFC files carry interoperable Property Sets and European Waste Catalogue classifications rather than proprietary labels, standardizing the audit deliverable. We evaluate the framework on a historical railway station in the Czech Republic, enabling a rare ex-post comparison against actual measured demolition tonnages. The comparison shows that the semantic enrichment pipeline itself introduced no measurable computational error: for the mineral fractions represented in the model, the predicted mass deviated by 28% from the measured tonnage, and the aggregate 51% gap between predicted and measured totals is attributable to materials outside the scope of the input geometry (subsurface, external, thin-layered, and non-structural elements) and to on-site re-sorting decisions rather than to the enrichment workflow. Hazardous chimney masonry identified and spatially localized in the model was separately dismantled according to the contractor, and no hazardous fraction appears in the demolition consignment records. Within the bounds of a single validated case and a dependence on the completeness of upstream reality capture, the results indicate that standardized, machine-readable pre-demolition audit deliverables are achievable today using exclusively open standards.

items.title: Building Deformation Simulation and Recognition via Localized Geometric Transformation and Collaborative Statistical Metrics
items.abstract: Building deformation, for example, tilting, settlement, and uplift, threatens structural safety, yet its rapid assessment is challenged by scarce real samples, subtle features, background clutter, and a lack of automated grading criteria. This study presents a task-specific computer vision framework integrating ROI-confined geometric simulation with multi-metric image-based assessment. For simulation, a localized geometric transformation applies rotation and vertical translation exclusively to the region of interest (ROI) of the building while preserving the background, generating eight deformation types with randomly sampled transformation magnitudes. For recognition, an edge-density-based strategy determines the building ROI from the reference image, and the same coordinates are used to crop the simulated image before pixel-wise differencing. A collaborative trio of metrics (SSIM, PSNR, and the threshold-exceeding pixel ratio) classifies deformations into four severity grades, each metric addressing a distinct distortion facet to provide complementary descriptions of image change. Evaluation using four building scenes and their synthetic deformation samples illustrates the spatial difference responses and metric-based screening outcomes under prescribed image transformations. The proposed approach offers a non-contact, cost-effective, and interpretable solution for routine building inspections and long-term health monitoring.

items.title: Who adopts where and when? Electric vehicle diffusion with building-level localization in Germany
Who adopts where and when? Electric vehicle diffusion with building-level localization in Germany
items.abstract: The electrification of private vehicles is a central element of decarbonizing transport and energy systems. Accurately anticipating when and where electric vehicles will be adopted is critical for charging infrastructure planning, distribution grid planning, and energy system operation, yet most diffusion models represent adoption at aggregated spatial scales. Here we introduce an open, scalable, high-resolution technology diffusion framework that links household-level electric vehicle adoption with georeferenced building-level residential locations. The framework combines a synthetic population, household-to-building matching, car ownership modeling, and a national Bass diffusion trajectory to translate aggregate electric vehicle growth into localized adoption pathways. We apply the framework to Germany from 2025 to 2050 and evaluate its main components using Census marginals, household-to-building consistency metrics, and registered vehicle counts, demonstrating its suitability for spatially explicit electric vehicle diffusion analysis. The results reveal substantial spatial heterogeneity in electric vehicle diffusion across regions, municipalities, grid cells, and buildings. Differences in household income and the share of single-family houses shape local adoption trajectories, leading to higher adoption in West Germany than in East Germany and slightly higher adoption in rural than urban municipalities in aggregate. The framework provides an open and transferable basis for spatially explicit modeling of household technology diffusion. Future research can build on these findings by applying the framework to other technologies or by linking electric vehicle diffusion at georeferenced building-level locations to charging demand, system operation, and infrastructure planning.

items.title: RTR-Align: Rule Token-to-Region Alignment for Construction Safety Violation Recognition and Localization
items.abstract: Construction safety inspections require identifying violated rules and localizing the associated workers or hazardous areas. Although multimodal large language models can describe hazards, supervision based solely on structured answers does not explicitly constrain the correspondence between rule records and visual targets. This study proposes RTR-Align, a Rule Token-to-Region Alignment method for construction safety violation recognition and localization. The method links the specific occurrence position of the Rule Token in each violation record to the corresponding target region, imposing separate spatial constraints on different instances associated with the same rule. It jointly learns rule assessment and target localization during LoRA adaptation of Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct. The study uses the ConstructionSite10k dataset, which contains 10,013 construction site images with violation question-answering and localization annotations, and produces instance-level annotations for training and evaluation by separating grouped instances, adjusting bounding-box boundaries, and adding annotations for missed targets. In the main run, RTR-Align achieved an F1 score of 62.72% and a total intersection over union (Total IoU) of 39.40% on the 3004 test images, exceeding the base model by 48.11 and 32.55 percentage points, respectively. RTR-Align produced fewer false positives than the base model, but its recall was 1.19 percentage points lower. Analyses across rules and scenarios, along with parameter and qualitative analyses, revealed performance differences and remaining challenges. These results support joint learning of violation recognition and rule-associated localization, enabling the model to identify relevant targets with fewer false positives and provide spatial evidence for manual verification.

items.title: Towards a preliminary model to assess the circularity potential of building materials at the product manufacturing stage:A systematic review
items.abstract: Purpose This study aims to develop a preliminary model to assess the circularity potential of building materials at the product manufacturing stage. Design/methodology/approach A PRISMA-guided systematic review analysed 148 peer-reviewed studies across five dimensions: study type, assessment scale, objective, methodological standardisation and scope. Descriptive analysis and a chi-square test identified patterns and relationships within the literature. The resulting research gaps were synthesised with evidence from 42 existing circularity assessment tools and a comparative analysis of BS EN 15804 and BS EN ISO 14051 to develop the preliminary model. Findings The literature is characterised by parallel development of established and novel methods but limited methodological consolidation. Assessment is concentrated at building and territorial scales; comparative sustainability assessment dominates and combined standardised and nonstandardised approaches remain uncommon. System boundaries also vary significantly with assessment scale. In response, the model establishes an A1-A3 product-stage boundary, disaggregates manufacturing through input-process-output mapping, and integrates qualitative circularity strategies with metrics for raw materials, energy and water across direct and indirect manufacturing flows. Research limitations and implications The model is derived from existing literature and has not yet been empirically validated. Several process and transportation-energy metrics require further operationalisation and testing with manufacturing data. Originality/value The study connects systematic literature review evidence directly to model development and combines a standardised A1-A3 product-stage boundary with process-level resource-flow visibility. It provides a transparent basis for developing a circularity-specific assessment of building-material manufacturing.

items.title: From Climate Risk Diagnosis to Design Decisions in the Built Environment: An Indicator-Based Adaptation Workflow with Bat-ADAPT and depthmapX
items.abstract: Climate adaptation in mixed-use building assets requires methods that connect class-based risk diagnosis with feasible design decisions and explicit spatial localisation, a link that remains weak in existing screening approaches. This paper develops and tests a lightweight, indicator-based workflow to address this gap. Bat-ADAPT (R4RE), an indicator-based climate-risk assessment tool, assesses exposure and vulnerability and derives cross-risk classes. It is also used to simulate adaptation packages. depthmapX, a space-syntax-based spatial analysis tool, provides a complementary layer for locating selected measures within shared outdoor spaces. The workflow is applied to Cascina Fossata in Turin, Italy, through two assessment profiles representing a reused historic courtyard building and a new multi-storey construction. The baseline diagnosis identifies Heat as the priority hazard and “Rainfall & Floods” as the second relevant condition. Under the final packages, Profile 1 vulnerability decreases from High to Medium for both hazards, while Profile 2 reaches Low vulnerability for Heat and Medium vulnerability for “Rainfall & Floods”. Exposure remains unchanged in both profiles. The depthmapX analysis informs the placement of visual risk communication and the identification of candidate locations for cool refuge areas. The intelligibility test yields R² = 0.0193 for the baseline configuration and R² = 0.9103 for the controlled alternative configuration, indicating a stronger relationship between Connectivity and Visual Integration for the tested geometry. The case study indicates that the workflow can provide a traceable basis for early-stage adaptation decisions, while its outputs remain class-based and the spatial results do not demonstrate climate-risk reduction.

items.title: Review on the Localized Construction of Modern Chinese New Nouns from the Perspective of Modern Enlightenment
items.abstract: The late Qing and early Republican periods were marked by profound transformations in Chinese society and language. With the spread of Western learning, numerous modern Western concepts entered traditional Chinese academia, promoting large-scale lexical renewal and semantic reshaping in Chinese. Against the background of modern ideological enlightenment, this paper focuses on the emergence, evolution and localization of modern Chinese new nouns. Adopting literature research and inductive analysis, it systematically reviews relevant academic studies drawn from scholarly databases. This study mainly explores two core issues: the major research dimensions and core academic viewpoints of existing research on modern new nouns,as well as the pathways through which new nouns emerge, evolve, and become localized in the context of modern enlightenment. The research concludes that the localization of modern Chinese new nouns is not only a lexical renovation process, but also a crucial driving force for modern Chinese ideological enlightenment, national consciousness shaping and social and cultural transformation.

items.title: The problem of the administrative-territorial delineation of Karachay autonomy in the process of nation-state building in the North Caucasus (1917-1926)
items.abstract: The purpose of the study is to identify patterns in the formation of Soviet statehood in Karachay in 1917-1926. The evolution of state government bodies – from the civil structures of the Provisional Government to autonomous entities within the RSFSR – is examined. Key factors of state-building are identified, including the impact of the policy of “War Communism” and the agrarian question. The scientific novelty of the article lies in introducing into scholarly discourse a number of archival documents of the South-Eastern Bureau of the Central Committee of the RCP(b) (Russian State Archive of Socio-Political History, f. 65, op. 1, d. 44, l. 110; d. 84, l. 29; d. 96, l. 18) that have not previously been drawn upon by researchers and reflect various viewpoints on the formation of national-state entities in the North Caucasus. Based on these materials, the reasons behind conflicts between ethnic groups and government authorities are substantiated. It is concluded that the establishment of the Karachay-Cherkess Autonomous Oblast was the result of a complex interplay between local initiatives of the national intelligentsia and the policy of the Soviet central government. It was established that the path of the Karachay people to statehood developed in stages: initially, the okrug functioned within the Mountain ASSR (January 1921 – January 1922), subsequently within the unified Karachay-Cherkess Autonomous Oblast (1922-1926), and the final step was delineation along national-territorial lines in 1926.

items.title: Assessing urban heat vulnerability in China's ten furnace cities through social sensing: Linking exposure, responses, and built environment
Artists Residencies for Architectural Quality of the Historic Coastal Landscape: Operational Guidelines for the Creative Regeneration of Built Environment
items.abstract: Historic coastal built heritage across Europe is increasingly exposed to multiple forms of degradation, shifting resulting from the anthropic and to environmental pressures. Interventions aimed at its reuse still struggle to reconcile regeneration requirements with the creative, social, and economic functions to keep these sites relevant to their communities. The Joint Declaration “Europe for Culture—Culture for Europe” (2026), and the European Commission provides a new shared culture and creative-led vision for interpreting regeneration processes as connection among individual, social, spatial, territorial, environmental, and institutional dimensions. This vision raises specific architectural and planning challenges: the need to reconcile overlapping heritage, landscape, and environmental protection regimes with the introduction of new creative and social functions, and to favour lightweight, reversible, and demountable interventions over permanent transformations. However, a gap lies in the lack of structured tools capable of guiding the creative regeneration of historic coastal built heritage under these constraints. While culture and creative-led regeneration, and adaptive reuse have been extensively investigated, the translation of creative regeneration principles into operational actions for the transformation of historic coastal built heritage into artist residencies remains insufficiently systematised into replicable design criteria for architectural and planning practice. Within this framework, the research aims to translate the aforementioned culture and creative-led vision into operational guidelines for improving the adaptive reuse of built heritage as artist residencies, providing a set of criteria that link European cultural-policy objectives to concrete architectural and planning actions for artist-in-residence adaptive reuse. The iterative methodology consists in three main phases: a knowledge phase, based on bibliometric and systematic analysis of t

items.title: BUILDING RESILIENCE THROUGH LOCALIZED CLIMATE ACTION WITHIN THE TOURISM SECTOR IN VICTORIA FALLS, ZIMBABWE
items.abstract: The way people live and collaborate within communities and cities can significantly impact efforts to address climate change. The use of energy-efficient buildings, low-carbon public transportation, and the encouragement of cycling and walking are all critical to reducing the carbon footprint. Greening cities with parks and gardens reduces carbon footprint, cools metropolitan areas, and reduces flooding. The paper examined how thinking and acting at a local level help communities fight climate change and build resilience to climate impacts. It discusses climate action and resilience efforts in Victoria Falls Town Council in Zimbabwe. The study employed a scoping review to map, report on, and identify knowledge gaps. The findings suggest that the majority of stakeholders are aware of the challenges posed by climate change. Several gaps have been identified in community engagement and in the implementation of sustainable practices. A few stakeholders have implemented energy-efficient building standards, invested in green spaces, and fostered public-private partnerships to fund climate action initiatives. Most tourism organisations have not yet adopted renewable energy, created green spaces to manage flood risks, or reduced the urban heat island effect. The study concluded that valuing local knowledge and strengthening community ties are crucial for fostering resilience against climate change impacts. The adoption of local climate-related strategies in tourism can safeguard the environment and improve local livelihoods. Thus, the paper underscores the significance of municipal budgets and public-private partnerships in localizing climate action in the tourism sector.

items.title: A Localized Seismic Shelter System (LSSS): A Dual- Structure Refuge for High-Rise Building Occupants
A LiDAR-visual-inertial odometry system for robust localization and RGB-colored mapping in construction sites
items.abstract: Robust localization and mapping are essential for autonomous inspection, progress monitoring, and digital documentation on construction sites. However, construction environments are typically unstructured, dynamic, and perceptually degraded, which poses significant challenges to existing odometry and mapping systems. This study develops a lightweight LiDAR-visual-inertial mapping system for construction environments by integrating a solid-state LiDAR with a visual camera using a FAST-LIVO2 framework. Two modules are introduced to enhance robustness: a degeneracy-aware adaptive weight adjustment module that reduces the influence of weak geometric constraints and degraded visual observations, and a dynamic object filtering module that suppresses moving-object-induced localization errors and ghosting artifacts in reconstructed maps. The system was validated through real-world experiments on active construction sites and benchmark evaluations under challenging scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can generate clean, RGB-colored 3D maps while maintaining robust localization in challenging construction environments.

items.title: Human Settlement in Mountains and Its Built Environment: Case Studies from the Caucasus Mountains between Local Pastoral Communities and Cross-regional States
items.abstract: The Caucasian mountain ranges of the Greater and Lesser Caucasus are highlands where people have been sedentary since the Neolithic period. Like in many of the mountains of western Eurasia, settlement oscillated between mobile and sedentary lifeways of the inhabitants, which goes hand in hand with very different forms of the built environment. Particularly in the Bronze and Iron Ages, complex pastoral settlement systems formed, culminating in the state-organized territorial structure of the Urartian kingdom, which partly was located in the South Caucasus. The chapter presents an overview of the organization of the Caucasian mountains as a habitat and domestic space used by mobile and semi-stationary pastoral peoples of the Bronze Age and by the sedentary and partly state-organized communities of the Early Iron Age. Using a case study from the North Caucasus, whose residential and economic architecture is exemplary for construction methods and techniques in high mountain regions, architectural environments and the elements that characterized built-up mountainscapes are discussed.

items.title: Durability-Informed End-of-Life Screening of Textile-Reinforced Mortar: Residual Performance, Degradation Localization, and Candidate Circular Pathways
items.abstract: Circular recovery decisions for aged strengthening systems require evidence that distinguishes loss of installed function from exhaustion of constituent value. Conventional durability studies rarely translate residual mechanical states into end-of-life decision support. This study develops an uncertainty-aware, multi-scale assessment for textile-reinforced mortar (TRM) based on three observed residual states: matrix retention (Rm), local pull-out/interface-related retention (Ri), and TRM-to-substrate/system-bond retention (Rb). AR-glass- and basalt-reinforced lime-based TRM systems were evaluated under dry reference, distilled-water, saline, alkaline, and acidic conditions after 1000, 3000, and 5000 h of exposure. Residual states were normalized to time-matched dry references, while 10,000 specimen-level bootstrap resamples quantified uncertainty. Cross-scale contrasts were used to identify degradation localization, and scenario thresholds of 0.60, 0.70, and 0.80 supported five performance-based end-of-life pathways. Among 24 non-reference conditions, 13 showed statistically supported localized or distributed degradation, whereas 11 remained uncertainty-dominated. At Rcrit=0.70, 12 conditions were classified as continued-service candidates, two as repair/rebonding candidates, seven as recovery-assessment candidates, none as material recycling/downcycling candidates, and three as requiring further inspection. At 5000 h, basalt-reinforced systems exposed to distilled water, alkaline, and acidic environments consistently exhibited a recovery-assessment pattern in which system-level functionality deteriorated while the observed lower-scale states remained comparatively preserved. No condition met the specific C4 material recycling/downcycling screening criteria under the tested states, thresholds, and decision rules, which means that those criteria were not satisfied and not that the materials are non-recyclable. Sensitivity analyses confirmed that alternative matrix de
