items.title: WebGIS for the 21st century: geoinformation, users, and public policy in the technical-scientific-informational milieu. From the invention of Geographic Information Systems to the construction of sociotechnical platforms for territorial justice and climat: From the invention of Geographic Information Systems to the construction of sociotechnical platforms for territorial justice and climate adaptation
items.venue: Universidade de São Paulo. Instituto de Arquitetura e Urbanismo eBooks
items.abstract: WebGIS for the 21st Century: Geoinformation, Users, and Public Policy in the Technical-Scientific-Informational Milieu propõe uma reconstrução histórica, epistemológica e aplicada da evolução dos Sistemas de Informação Geográfica, desde os primeiros sistemas computacionais destinados ao planejamento territorial até a emergência de plataformas WebGIS capazes de articular dados, usuários, instituições, interpretação territorial e políticas públicas. A obra parte de uma pergunta fundamental: o que deve ser um WebGIS no século XXI? Para respondê-la, o livro recupera a origem dos SIG na década de 1960, especialmente a experiência canadense do Canada Land Inventory e o trabalho pioneiro de Roger Tomlinson, mostrando como os primeiros GIS surgiram quando o volume e a complexidade das informações territoriais excederam a capacidade de processamento manual. O mapa deixa, então, de ser apenas um produto gráfico e passa a integrar um sistema de dados, consultas, classificações, cruzamentos e modelos destinados a apoiar decisões territoriais. A partir dessa genealogia, o livro examina a transformação da cartografia analógica em sistemas computacionais de representação espacial. Pontos, linhas, polígonos, matrizes raster, redes, atributos e bancos de dados passam a constituir formas de codificação do território. Essa transformação amplia extraordinariamente a capacidade analítica, mas também introduz um problema epistemológico decisivo: a representação computacional não é a própria realidade territorial. Toda camada, indicador, modelo ou mapa decorre de escolhas teóricas, metodológicas, técnicas e políticas. Inspirado na contribuição de Milton Santos e da Geografia Crítica, o livro sustenta que o espaço não pode ser reduzido a uma superfície ou a uma coleção de objetos georreferenciados. Ele deve ser entendido como uma totalidade produzida pela relação entre sistemas de objetos e sistemas de ações, envolvendo fluxos, lugares, infraestruturas, normas, conflitos, desigualdades, in

items.title: Urban socio-territorial movements
items.abstract: This chapter analyzes the MOI (Movement of Renters and Occupiers), an Argentine social movement that fights for access to housing through the self-managed social production of habitat in Buenos Aires. From a critical geographical perspective, the authors characterize it as an urban socio-territorial movement, given that the appropriation of territory is central to its political project. The study explores four analytical dimensions in territorial terms: strategy, identity, political socialization, and institutions. Drawing on fieldwork conducted in 2024–2025, it examines how the MOI builds “territories for life” outside market logic, producing collective housing at costs 30–40% lower than commercial construction. The authors conclude that these movements propose an alternative urban habitability paradigm grounded in self-management, collective ownership, and solidarity, challenging the neoliberal model that dominates Argentine housing policy.

items.title: Thermal descriptor extraction through reciprocal residual attention learning for construction worker unsafe condition detection and localization
items.abstract: Unsafe worker actions in elevated construction environments remain a leading cause of occupational accidents, particularly under low-visibility and complex environmental conditions where conventional RGB-based monitoring systems exhibit limited robustness. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel Thermal Context-Guided Dual-path Reciprocal Network (TCDRNet) for intelligent detection of unsafe thermal actions. Initially, a novel Thermal Adaptive Gradient (TAG) preprocessing filter is introduced to enhance thermal image quality via local normalisation, gradient-based thermal boundary enhancement, adaptive thermal weighting, feature amplification, and edge-preserving smoothing. The generated TAG images are subsequently processed utilising the proposed TCDRNet, which incorporates a Cross Stage Partial Dual-path Reciprocal Network (CSPDRNet) backbone integrated with Thermal Global Descriptor Extraction (TGDE), Reciprocal Attention Generation (RAG), and Residual Reciprocal Fusion (RRF) modules to facilitate reciprocal thermal feature learning. Furthermore, Spatial Pyramid Pooling (SPP) is employed for multi-scale contextual extraction. Concurrently, the Path Aggregation Network (PANet) performs hierarchical feature aggregation to generate low-level localisation features, mid-level boundary information, and high-level semantic representations. Finally, a Thermal Context-Aware Residual Attention (TAR) module is introduced to refine the multi-scale features via channel attention, spatial attention, and residual fusion, thereby emphasising discriminative unsafe regions. Experimental evaluation on a thermal unsafe action dataset comprising no-helmet, no-shoes, mobile-phone utilisation, safe and unsafe posture classes demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed framework. TCDRNet achieves an accuracy of 96.60%, precision of 96.41%, and recall of 95.96%, outperforming several state-of-the-art models.

items.title: Tunnel Convergence in Squeezing Ground with Strain Localisation
items.abstract: Modelling strain-softening behaviour in rocks and hard clays presents significant challenges due to strain localisation, which may lead to non-unique and mesh-dependent numerical solutions. In engineering practice, computationally tractable alternatives are therefore often used, including softening models suppressing strain localisation (hereafter referred to as non-localised softening analyses) or perfectly plastic models based on residual strength (hereafter referred to as perfectly plastic residual-strength analyses). Their adequacy for predicting unsupported tunnel convergence under squeezing conditions is investigated through comparative numerical computations using a conventional, non-regularised strain-softening model. The study covers a wide range of softening parameters and problem layouts, including circular and horseshoe-shaped tunnels under isotropic and anisotropic stress fields, as well as spatial discretisations based on structured and unstructured meshes. The finest structured mesh had boundary elements as small as 12 mm and produced numerical shear bands with thicknesses of the same order as those seen experimentally; the corresponding results are used as pragmatic reference solutions. The results show that a distinction must be made between average and local maximum convergence. For the rotationally symmetric tunnel problem, the perfectly plastic residual-strength model may underestimate local maxima; in the structured-mesh study, the underestimation reached about 30%, while the unstructured analyses showed that point-wise maxima are sensitive to mesh topology and symmetry assumptions. For the non-rotationally symmetric layouts examined, however, the model was conservative with respect to local maxima. The model predicted average convergence closely, although moderate underestimation occurred in some cases. This is the main practical result: average or diametral convergence usually governs design, whereas local maxima matter for concentrated suppor

items.title: The Reconstruction of the Security Mechanism and Smart Governance in China : Building an Analytical Framework through Contemporary Reconfiguration and Localization
items.abstract: 본 논문은 디지털 기반 거버넌스의 세계적 수렴 경향에 주목함과 동시에, 각 지역의 맥락적 특수성이 반영된 통치 양상을 입체적으로 분석할 수 있는 분석의 틀을 구축하고자 한다. 본 연구는 스마트 거버넌스를 새로운 기술 기반의 통치 방식으로 이해하기보다, 근대 자유주의 통치가 지속적으로 직면해 온 자유와 안전 사이의 긴장을 기술적 수단을 통해 조절하려는 통치 시도로 파악한다. 기존 연구가 스마트 거버넌스를 감시나 효율성이라는 기술적 효과의 상반된 측면에 주목해 온 것과 달리, 본 논문은 기술 중심 거버넌스의 등장과 작동을 가능하게 한 역사적·맥락적 조건에 주목한다. 이를 위해 미셸 푸코의 통치성 이론, 특히 안전 메커니즘 개념을 첨단 기술 조건에서 재구성하고, 데이터 및 알고리즘에 기반한 스마트 거버넌스를 ‘기술 결합적 현대 안전 메커니즘’으로 규정한다. 나아가 본 논문은 기술 중심 통치가 심화한 중국의 사례를 통해, 이러한 분석틀이 특정 지역 맥락과 결합해 구체적 통치 양상으로 지역화되는 과정을 드러낸다. 특히 팬데믹 시기 중국의 실제 기술 중심 통치 실천을 참조해, 개혁개방 이후 자유의 공간과 당 중심의 권위가 교차하는 중국 특유의 혼종적 작동 방식을 포착할 수 있는 분석틀을 정식화한다. 이는 향후 여러 지역 맥락에서 전개되는 디지털 거버넌스의 양상을 탐색하기 위한 분석적 기초가 될 것이다.

Fully Deterministic Shallow Neural Networks with Localized Activations. Part I: Construction and Optimal Sobolev Approximation

For each $s>0$, explicit deterministic rules prescribe all hidden parameters independently of the target $u\in H^s(Ω)$. At frequency resolution $M$, the $N_M\asymp M^d$ prescribed features span a linear space $V_M$. For every sufficiently large integer $N$, we choose $M\asymp N^{1/d}$ with $N_M\le N$ and construct a bounded linear operator $A_N:H^s(Ω)\to V_M$ such that \[ \|u-A_Nu\|_{H^m(Ω)} \le C N^{-(s-m)/d}\|u\|_{H^s(Ω)} \] for every $u\in H^s(Ω)$ and every integer $0\le m

items.title: Circular Strategies for Handling Greywater
items.abstract: This chapter offers a comprehensive examination of greywater, highlighting its characteristics and its role in sustainable water management. Greywater is generally understood as wastewater produced from household activities like laundry, dishwashing, and bathing, and it has unique properties that set it apart from blackwater. While greywater presents significant opportunities for resource recovery, it can also pose environmental challenges and health risks if not properly treated. The chapter underscores the value of decentralized greywater treatment systems, which allow for localized water management and recycling, thereby alleviating pressure on centralized treatment facilities. Furthermore, recovering resources such as nutrients and energy from greywater enhances the sustainability of the water cycle. Integrating greywater management within a circular economy framework is crucial for reducing waste and optimizing resource use. This strategy encourages water reuse, ultimately promoting environmental sustainability and resilience in urban areas.

items.title: A Variable-Receptive-Field Model for Joint Radio Map Construction and Radiation Source Localization in Urban Environments
items.abstract: With the growing demand for smart-city electromagnetic monitoring, radiation source localization based on received signal strength indication (RSSI) remains challenging in complex urban environments because RSSI measurements are affected by non-line-of-sight propagation, multipath fading, and shadow fading. Motivated by this challenge, we design a lightweight autoencoder named LocAutoencoder to jointly perform radio map construction and radiation source localization in urban environments. In the encoder, a variable-receptive-field module uses multiple dilation rates to extract multi-scale wireless propagation features directly from both RSSI measurements and urban map information. The sequential dilated convolutions expand the receptive field without substantially increasing the parameter count. In the decoder, a dual-task decoder is designed with two output branches: one branch reconstructs the radio map, whereas the other estimates the source coordinate through probability heatmap generation and centroid calculation. The lightweight autoencoder model computes the probability-weighted centroid within the network to directly output the estimated coordinates, enabling accurate estimation of the radiation source location without requiring a separate localization subnetwork. Finally, simulations and comparative experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed network in terms of localization accuracy, robustness, and computational efficiency.

items.title: Robust Localization of Autonomous Excavators via EKF-Based Sensor Fusion in Real-World Construction Environments
items.abstract: Reliable localization is a prerequisite for autonomous excavation, yet outdoor construction environments introduce GNSS degradation, vibration, and terrain-induced slip that can compromise single-sensor estimates. This study reports the implementation and field evaluation of an EKF-based localization system that fuses Global Navigation Satellite System-Real-Time Kinematics (GNSS-RTK), inertial measurement unit (IMU), and encoder measurements within a robot operating system (ROS) pipeline for an autonomous excavator. The fusion strategy weights complementary sensor measurements according to modeled uncertainty and down-weights GNSS updates classified as degraded. Experimental evaluation on a mapped outdoor route shows that the fused trajectory remains stable under non-ideal operating conditions, including signal obstructions and high-vibration segments. The EKF-fused trajectory achieved a path-deviation RMSE of 0.139 m and a P95 path deviation of 0.213 m relative to the independently surveyed reference path. These results support the feasibility of probabilistic multi-sensor fusion for autonomous excavation tasks in challenging field environments.

items.title: The $J$-Homomorphism From Localising The Cobordism Hypothesis
items.abstract: Lurie's cobordism hypothesis classifies fully extended framed topological field theories valued in a symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathcal{C}$ with duals by the $\infty$-groupoid $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$ of fully dualisable objects. This classification results in an $O(n)$-action on $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$, where $O(n)$ acts on the framed bordism category by change of framing. Lurie observed that for a connective spectrum, this action is ``a version of the classical $J$-homomorphism.'' We make this identification explicit: with respect to the right action of $O(n)$ on framings, the $O(n)$-action on the localisation $L(\mathrm{Bord}_n^{\mathrm{fr}}) \simeq S$ is precisely $\ominus J_n$, the inverse of the unstable $J$-homomorphism $J_n \colon O(n) \to \mathrm{GL}_1(S)$. The identification of the action with the unstable $J$-homomorphism in the setting of smooth stacks is due to Grady--Pavlov; we give an independent proof in Lurie's original formulation of the cobordism hypothesis, using the abstract Pontryagin--Thom construction. The sign (i.e.\ whether the action is $J_n$ or $\ominus J_n$) depends on the convention for the $O(n)$-action on framings, and is relevant for $\mathrm{pin}^\pm$ theories and hence for quantum systems with time-reversal symmetry. We compute the induced action on homotopy groups of the sphere spectrum in low degrees, yielding explicit invariants for invertible TFTs in dimensions $1$, $2$, and $3$, and connect these to the Kitaev chain, the framing anomaly, the spin-statistics theorem, and anomaly inflow. We recover the Galatius--Madsen--Tillmann--Weiss theorem as a consequence of the cobordism hypothesis and relate the homotopy fixed-point and mapping-spectrum perspectives on invertible TFTs via the duality between tangential and normal framings.

items.title: Preventing negative transfer in cross-building Wi-Fi fingerprint localization via validation-gated estimator selection
items.abstract: Cross-building transfer learning can reduce Wi-Fi fingerprint calibration effort, but it may degrade positioning when source and target environments have incompatible access-point deployments, propagation conditions, or spatial mappings. This paper proposes SafeTransLoc, a framework that treats transfer as an optional deployment decision: target-only and transfer candidates are compared on held-out target data, and transfer is accepted only when its validation advantage exceeds a safety margin. The principal UJIIndoorLoc and SODIndoorLoc evaluation comprises 120 cross-building configurations; under the deployment-level criterion, the best transfer candidate was worse than the strongest target-only alternative in all of them. A post-review controlled same-environment SODIndoorLoc experiment adds 270 RSS-offset/noise configurations and yields 6 beneficial-transfer and 264 harmful-transfer cases. With a zero margin, the gate accepted 1 of the 6 beneficial cases and rejected 89.0% of harmful transfers; increasing the margin improved harmful-transfer rejection but reduced beneficial-transfer sensitivity. Independent leave-one-environment-out calibration on the archived SOD results selected 0 m for CETC331 and 0.5 m for HCXY and SYL, producing one held-out false acceptance overall. These results support SafeTransLoc as a deployment safeguard while showing that conservative validation gating involves a measurable safety-sensitivity trade-off under sparse target supervision.

items.title: Non-adiabatic Optimisation via Localisation-Delocalisation Transitions
items.abstract: The promise of efficiently solving classical optimisation problems on quantum computers is tantalizing. As many such problems can be mapped to approximating the ground state of spin-glasses, paradigmatic models for studying many-body localisation, it is natural to ask if some of the intuition coming from quantum statistical mechanics can help guide the construction of novel quantum optimisation algorithms. In this work, we discuss how continuous reverse quantum annealing crossing a many-body localisation transition can be accelerated by considering the density of Landau-Zener crossings as the system is quenched. We provide an interpretation of this behaviour in terms of an effective Fokker-Planck equation for the success probability of the algorithm. This interpretation suggests an improvement in the required annealing time as a function of the system size $N$, which goes from $\mathcal{O}({\rm poly}(N))$ to $\mathcal{O}(1)$ for reference states with non-vanishing energy density. We show that the continuous dynamics can be Trotterised with a number of steps that remains modest as system size increases, making it appealing for near-term devices. For the resulting circuit implementation, we provide a quantitative strategy for determining the parameters of the time-dependent Hamiltonian. We compare the performance of our digitised algorithm, which we call FRIO, against that of the QAOA for finding the ground state of spin-glass problems, in particular the SK model. The numerical results suggest that with suitably selected circuit parameters which can be efficiently found using thermalizing dynamics, FRIO almost always outperforms the conventional QAOA ansatz with pre-optimized angles.

items.title: Direction-Robust UAV–Satellite Cross-View Geo-Localization via Spatial Adaptive Alignment and Circular Adjacent-Direction Gated Interaction
items.abstract: Cross-view geo-localization (CVGL) matches unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) images with geotagged satellite imagery to support visual localization in Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-challenged environments. However, substantial cross-view discrepancies between UAV and satellite images, together with variations in UAV viewing direction, induce pronounced shifts in feature distributions, thereby undermining the stability of cross-view matching. To address these issues, we propose a progressive spatial-to-directional framework. The Spatial Adaptive Alignment Module first adaptively balances height–channel and width–channel responses and applies a fine-grained consistency constraint to reduce cross-view feature discrepancies. On the spatially adapted features, the Direction-Aware Module performs radial directional decomposition and organizes the resulting directional features into a circularly ordered sequence. A channel-wise gated interaction mechanism then selectively transfers information between each direction and its circularly adjacent neighbors after semantic-space projection. This local interaction captures gradual structural transitions between neighboring directions while preserving direction-specific discriminability and avoiding indiscriminate global mixing. Across three independent training runs on University-1652, our method achieves mean R@1 and AP values of 94.63% and 95.46% for UAV-to-satellite retrieval. The corresponding means for satellite-to-UAV retrieval are 96.86% and 93.97%. These results demonstrate that our method effectively improves UAV–satellite cross-view retrieval performance and maintains stable retrieval performance under different UAV viewing directions.

items.title: Transformation of the Kingly State in Consanguineous-Territorial Relations
items.abstract: This chapter examines how competition and change during the Spring and Autumn Period further broke Chinese ancestors away from the bondage of long-standing consanguineous gentile society. The evolution of human society is a continuous process of differentiation from the whole to the individual. The state was born out of division and exists because of the integration of a divided society. However, the early monarchic state, modeled on narrow blood relations and centered on the king and his royal clan, could not bear the political integration function for vast territories with diverse ethnic groups. Thus, society entered a stage of re-differentiation in the form of a state. The division of the Western Zhou and Eastern Zhou resembles brothers splitting up and going their separate ways. The king’s rule could not be maintained without division, and division inevitably led to competition, in which all sides sought change. “Competition” and “change” became the theme of the era. The chapter explores this transformative process through eight dimensions: iron and fire in building a prosperous country with a powerful army; the rise of vassal states and clashes among feudal princes; rivals and the accumulation of power; the emergence of the administrative system and the territorial state; the tension between kinship and talents; the construction of publicness and civilization; the eventual prevalence of the State of Qin as the latecomer wins; and finally, the Tao and the Entity in homogeneous competition.

items.title: Localised Fibre Reinforcement for Bearing Regions in 3D Printed Composites
items.venue: Advances in engineering research/Advances in Engineering Research
items.abstract: This study investigates the influence of localised continuous fibre toolpaths on the structural behaviour of additive manufactured composite components containing geometric defects.Using a Markforged platform, 40-layer symmetrical specimens (𝑂𝑛𝑦𝑥 4 /𝐺𝐹 32 /𝑂𝑛𝑦𝑥 4 ) were manufactured with a central 6 mm hole.Three distinct configurations were evaluated to assess fibre architecture variations: a baseline quasi-isotropic layout (G1), and two architectures reinforced with 2 (G2) and 4 (G3) concentric circular fibre paths around the hole boundary.Classical Laminate Theory was used to establish the global laminate stiffness, while a geometric reinforcement model quantified local circumferential fibre continuity surrounding the hole, yielding a uniform global in-plane stiffness of 8.76 GPa.Analytical results indicate that while the localised rings result in a negligible global fibre volume variation (Δ𝑉 𝑓 = 0.10%), they significantly enhance geometric fibre path continuity adjacent to the defect (138.23 mm in G3 compared to 0 mm in G1).This localised continuity is hypothesised to optimise stress distribution and load transfer mechanisms under complex bearing stress fields, establishing a predictive analytical framework for subsequent experimental validation.

items.title: Structured Chain-of-Thought with Self-Correction for Training-Free Damage Grading of Pre-Localized Buildings Using Qwen3-VL-30B
items.abstract: Accurate mapping of building damage after destructive natural disasters is essential for emergency response and recovery planning. However, annotated post-disaster samples are often scarce, and conventional supervised models usually generalize poorly across scenes and hazard types. These constraints limit the operational use of remote sensing-based damage assessment during emergency response. To address this problem, this study proposes SCTSC-VLM, a training-free framework for damage grading of pre-localized building instances, implemented using a locally deployed Q4_K_M 4-bit quantized version of the Qwen3-VL-30B vision–language model. The framework has three main components. First, an instance-level visual input construction strategy integrates independent assessment of building instances localized by the supplied footprint data without a dedicated instance segmentation model. Second, a hierarchical reasoning mechanism decomposes the assessment into four progressive stages: multi-view structured feature extraction, independent visual description, cross-validation, and rule-constrained classification. This design is intended to reduce hallucination and visually ungrounded reasoning. Third, a multi-sampling ensemble decision mechanism mitigates the randomness of autoregressive generation. The framework was evaluated using post-disaster optical imagery from the 2025 Dingri earthquake and the 2025 Eaton Fire in California. On the full Dingri evaluation dataset comprising Areas A–C (n = 398), SCTSC-VLM achieved a Macro-F1 score of 88.2% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.806. On the separate full California evaluation dataset (n = 386), it achieved a Macro-F1 score of 83.8% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.800. Separate ablation experiments were conducted on explicitly defined analysis populations to examine the contributions of the framework components. In both full-dataset evaluations, the fully damaged and undamaged classes obtained higher F1-scores than the partially damaged

items.title: Construction of a localized conceptual framework for nursing death education from the perspective of traditional Chinese medicine philosophy on life and death
items.venue: DOAJ (DOAJ: Directory of Open Access Journals)
items.abstract: ObjectiveAddressing the reliance of Chinese nursing death education on Western theoretical frameworks,its limited cultural adaptability,and the insufficient translation of indigenous wisdom into educational practice,this study proposed a localized conceptual framework grounded in traditional Chinese medicine(TCM) philosophy on life and death.MethodsIntegrating a literature synthesis with hermeneutic analysis of classical TCM texts,we reviewed current research paradigms and theoretical limitations in nursing death education.By analyzing classical discourses on life and death,core philosophical propositions were distilled to construct a localized educational framework alongside corresponding implementation pathways and evaluation systems.ResultsA total of 4 core philosophical propositions were systematically derived:the unity of life and death,the coexistence of physical form and spirit,the natural lifespan perspective,and end⁃of⁃life medical ethics.Based on these,a conceptual framework was established featuring four progressive instructional units:cognitive restructuring of death,integrated physical⁃spiritual care,peaceful transition at life's end,and bereavement support-complemented by tiered implementation pathways and a mixed quantitative⁃qualitative evaluation scheme.ConclusionsThis framework provides a theoretical foundation and actionable guidance for localizing nursing death education,bridging the cultural alignment gap in existing paradigms.Its practical utility warrants further validation through expert consensus and empirical educational research.

items.title: A critical methodology for education monitoring in Lebanon: Localising and institutionalising research
items.abstract: This paper examines the establishment, purpose and methodologies of the Education Monitor in Lebanon as a methodological intervention towards localising research on education in emergencies. Led by the Centre for Lebanese Studies, the Monitor was designed to create a sustained, independent research agenda outside donor-driven project cycles. Emphasising institutionalisation and beginnings in research, this paper critically reflects on the processes of building localised knowledge production. The Monitor combines annual quantitative online surveys with qualitative interviews to track education amid Lebanon’s compounded crises. This paper reflects on five years of establishing infrastructure, ensuring data accessibility to local stakeholders and the challenges of representativity. We demonstrate how institutionalised, incremental research can shift power in knowledge production towards more localised research practices and as a tool for addressing educational injustice.

items.title: Lessons in localising a climate-resilient development pathways (CRDPs) approach
items.abstract: The Tuwe Pamoja project worked to strengthen the capacities of city actors to plan and implement climate resilient nature-based solutions that are locally driven, effective, and equitable for all urban residents. Partners across the four African cities - Cape Town, Lusaka, Nairobi and Accra - focussed on building capacities to localise a climate-resilient development pathways (CRDPs) approach. CRDPs are accumulated sets of measures implemented over time that that make settlements and those that live and work in them safer in the face of climate extreme events, like floods, droughts, heatwaves and wildfires. This learning brief shares how we used various methods to animate engagements between community leaders, residents, staff of civil society organisations, researchers and government officials on what development pathways have shaped the specific informal settlements we are working in and what practical changes would make the development pathway more climate resilient, especially in the face of flooding. Together, we considered various types of interventions and practices, paying particular attention to nature-based solutions. We share five emerging lessons.

items.title: Mapping the territorial politics of data centre opposition
items.abstract: Despite growing scholarly interest in data centres, opposition to their construction has so far been studied mainly through single cases, and rarely through a geographical lens. This commentary addresses that gap by presenting an original dataset of around seventy documented cases of mobilisation against data centre projects across Europe, the United States, Latin America, Asia, and Africa. Comparing these cases across macro-regions, the commentary identifies the main cross-cutting patterns of contention and identifies a recurring spatial patterns, while laying the empirical groundwork for future theoretical explanations of the observed variation.

items.title: Unravelling the differentiated effects of the block built environment on PM2.5 concentrations: A new research framework based on the perspective of source-flow-sink
Tribal Kingly States in Consanguineous-Territorial Relations
items.abstract: This chapter examines the origin of the state in both temporal and spatial dimensions. Drawing on the Marxist theory of state origin—including the three general ideas derived from Athens, Rome, and Germany—the chapter argues that while most early states emerged from secondary relations as exemplified by ancient Athens, the pristine state followed a different path. Due to a lack of sufficient empirical materials from China’s earliest period, the chapter takes ancient Athens as a productive reference rather than a direct comparison. This approach reveals that the pristine state was formed on the basis of human primordial relations, namely blood relations, rather than territorial divisions. The chapter then traces the making of the state through war and agriculture, giving rise to a dynastic state born in consanguineous relationships. It further examines kingly states within the framework of familial domination, the process of nation-state-building, the tension between territorial expansion and consanguineous connections, the coexistence of dynastic and gentile affairs, and finally, the ancestral integration of kingly states. By reconstructing this distinct origin path, the chapter provides a foundational understanding of how blood-based relations shaped the earliest form of the state in China.

items.title: SIT-ANTOFAGASTA: TOOL FOR DECENTRALIZED TERRITORIAL PLANNING
items.venue: Revista Geográfica de Chile Terra Australis
items.abstract: Decentralization in Chile has sought to strengthen regional autonomy and improve the efficiency of public management; however, its implementation has been slow and fragmented, with persistent territorial gaps and limitations in subnational capacities. In this context, the article analyzes the Territorial Information System of Antofagasta (SIT-Antofagasta) as a sociotechnical infrastructure that articulates geospatial data, actors, and planning instruments to support territorial governance and regional decentralization. Using methods that combine documentary analysis, interviews with key stakeholders, and geospatial examples, the study examines its operation, governance model, practical applications, and contribution to evidence-based decision-making. The results show that SIT-Antofagasta facilitates the territorialization of the Sustainable Development Goals, strengthens transparency and participation, and contributes to reducing urban–rural gaps through the generation and democratization of information at the local scale, highlighting the case of the Observatorio Salar de Atacama. Furthermore, the role of capacity building and multi-actor collaboration in the system’s sustainability is evidenced. Despite limitations related to costs, technical capacities, and data updating, SIT-Antofagasta is consolidated as a replicable model for sustainable territorial planning and decentralized governance in contexts of regional inequality in Chile.

items.title: From Sensing to Transforming: An AI-Enabled Capability Framework for Circular Construction and Demolition Waste Management
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and AI-enabled digital technologies are increasingly proposed as enablers of circularity in construction and demolition (C&D) waste management, yet existing reviews are organised around technology and lifecycle stage and rarely examine the organisational conditions under which technically capable applications move from pilot to sustained practice. This review addresses that gap through a PRISMA 2020-guided systematic review of 217 recent Scopus records (2022–2026), interpreted through dynamic capabilities theory, diffusion of innovation theory, and the circular economy value-retention hierarchy. Abstract-level coding of capability enablers, AI mechanism clusters, and circularity outcomes is triangulated with latent Dirichlet allocation topic modelling, bibliographic coupling, co-citation and keyword co-occurrence analyses, and statistical tests of association. The central finding concerns where research attention has concentrated: digital infrastructure and AI/machine learning technical capability appear in 64–67% of studies, whereas governance and human/organisational capability appear in only 13–18%, and traceability/material security is the least-examined outcome (11.1%). These patterns describe the published literature rather than organisational practice. They are integrated into a four-layer framework that separates observed associations from theoretical inferences, and into six propositions for organisational-level testing. Substantive policy instruments appear in only 4.1% of studies, so the policy implications are presented as exploratory.

items.title: From Material Recovery to Circular Valorization in Construction and Demolition Waste Management: Evidence and a Circular Valorization Framework from a Brazilian Recycling Facility
items.abstract: Construction and Demolition Waste (CDW) recycling is essential for circular economy strategies, yet material recovery alone does not demonstrate effective circular valorization. This study investigates how a CDW recycling facility can progress from conventional waste recovery toward measurable, traceable, and sustainability-oriented circular resource management. An exploratory-descriptive single-case study was conducted in Porto Rico, Paraná, Brazil, based on systematic direct observation and documentary, operational, and commercialization records. The facility processes approximately 24 000 t of CDW annually, converting concrete and brick waste into recycled gravel, wood into chips for thermal energy applications, and redirecting other recyclable fractions to external recovery chains. Commercialization data for 2022–2023 showed a 5.2% decrease in recycled-gravel sales and a 310.3% increase in other recovered-material volumes, although substantial temporal concentration and variability were observed. The findings reveal circularity gaps related to incomplete material-flow measurement, aggregated records, limited material characterization, market continuity, traceability, and information integration. These results demonstrate that circular performance depends not only on material recovery but also on material quality, value retention, market reinsertion, and measurable resource flows. Based on these empirical gaps, an empirically grounded, case-derived Circular CDW Valorization Framework and a Circular Performance Measurement Architecture are proposed, linking material-flow measurement, material quality, value retention, market development, sustainability indicators, and targeted digital enablement. The study advances the distinction between circular practices and circular performance and provides a structured pathway from waste diversion and material recovery toward measurable and traceable circular resource management.

items.title: Advancing Circular Economy Innovation: A Multi‐Criteria Tool for Evaluating Construction Materials
items.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
items.abstract: The construction industry is a major consumer of raw materials and a significant contributor to environmental impacts, highlighting the importance of circular material selection. This study presents a structured framework for assessing construction materials based on circular economy (CE) criteria to support informed and transparent decision‐making. A three‐phase methodology was adopted, comprising criteria prioritisation, rubric development and validation, and material‐level assessment using evidence from peer‐reviewed literature. Eleven CE criteria were weighted through expert judgement and applied using a validated multi‐criteria rubric to evaluate 10 commonly used construction materials. The findings reveal clear variation in circular performance across materials. Cross‐Laminated Timber achieved the highest overall weighted circularity score (4.15), driven by strong performance in reusability, non‐toxic properties, and embodied carbon, while conventional materials such as PVC pipes recorded the lowest score (2.80), primarily due to poor reusability and disassembly performance despite high availability and market maturity. These results demonstrate that end‐of‐life value retention and lifecycle circularity are more influential than market‐driven factors in determining material circularity. The proposed assessment framework offers a robust and evidence‐based tool for circular material selection in the construction industry.

items.title: Circular economy assessment of biomethane value chain in Brazil
items.abstract: From the numerous opportunities to add value to biomass in Brazil, biomethane production in sugarcane mills presents significant potential. This study introduces a diagnostic framework grounded in circular economy (CE) principles to assess new biomethane projects, aligning with the strategic objectives of product diversification, full biomass utilization, circularity, and regional integration. By adopting seven CE principles to qualitatively and quantitatively evaluate systemic impacts, the assessment provides a flexible tool for visualizing and testing alternative biorefinery configurations during the feasibility stage. The framework is applied to two real‐world scenarios: (i) the on‐site replacement of diesel in agricultural and transport operations; and (ii) the regional commercialization of biomethane via pipeline to substitute industrial liquefied petroleum gas (LPG). Results indicate that both pathways achieve over 85% reduction in carbon intensity compared with fossil benchmarks, while simultaneously enhancing nutrient cycling and soil regeneration through improved digestate application. The CE‐based assessment further demonstrates that on‐site utilization fosters internal transactional efficiency and operational control, whereas regional distribution extends defossilization benefits throughout the broader industrial value chain. The framework facilitates strategic decision‐making by capturing dimensions of value retention, regeneration, and stakeholder collaboration within bio‐based systems. This approach serves as a replicable and complementary tool for evaluating diverse bioeconomy contexts, supporting the transition toward more circular and resilient regional systems.

items.title: Circular Economy Practices and Sustainable Performance: An Empirical Study
items.abstract: This study examines the extent to which basic and advanced circular economy practices are associated in different ways with the environmental, economic and social dimensions of sustainable performance at the firm level. Starting from the premise that the circular economy should not be treated as a homogeneous construct, the study distinguishes between more operational practices, geared towards efficiency and waste reduction, and more transformational practices, associated with redesign, value retention and the reconfiguration of value creation and capture models. Empirically, a quantitative, cross‐sectional, organisation‐level design is adopted, based on 255 companies operating in Portugal. The data were analysed using descriptive statistics, reliability tests, bivariate correlations and hierarchical ordinary least squares regressions. The results show that basic circular economy practices exhibit positive, robust and consistent associations with environmental performance and economic performance, emerging as the empirically strongest core of circular value creation. The environmental dimension proves to be the aspect of sustainable performance most directly sensitive to the adoption of these practices. In contrast, although advanced practices show positive associations in intermediate models, they do not demonstrate a robust incremental contribution to economic and social performance in the full models. The study contributes to the literature by emphasising the need to distinguish between different types of circular practices, by linking the debate on the circular economy to the literature on strategy and sustainability and by offering a more nuanced understanding of multidimensional sustainable performance. items.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the Circular Economy: A Systematic Literature Review
items.abstract: The transition from linear production and consumption to a circular economy (CE) requires organizations to manage complex information about products, materials, waste streams, and supply-chain activities. Artificial intelligence (AI) may support this transition, but research on its role across business and organizational contexts remains fragmented. This study systematically reviews how AI is applied to CE practices and identifies the main thematic areas in the literature. Following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement, Scopus was searched for English-language studies published up to 2025. After screening 301 records and assessing 56 full texts, 25 studies were included and analyzed through qualitative content analysis and thematic narrative synthesis. Four clusters emerged: AI-enabled circular operations and supply-chain transformation; resource recirculation, recovery, and loop closure; organizational and ecosystem capabilities for circular innovation and business-model transformation; and green marketing, stakeholder engagement, and corporate disclosure. Across these clusters, AI is reported primarily to improve visibility, prediction, classification, optimization, and coordination. Evidence is strongest for operational efficiency and waste-related applications, while support for higher-value circular strategies and system-level loop closure remains limited. AI should therefore be regarded as a conditional enabler rather than a sufficient driver of circular transformation; its contribution depends on circular objectives, organizational capabilities, human expertise, infrastructure, financing, governance, and interorganizational cooperation.

items.title: Hospicing the Linear Economy: Care-Ethical Exnovation in Circular Economy Transitions
items.abstract: Circular economy scholarship increasingly recognises circularity as a social, ethical, and place-based transformation alongside material-loop closure. This paper develops Hospice Work for the Linear Economy as a care-ethical framework for accompanying the decline of linear practices, infrastructures, identities, and dependencies within circular transitions. Bringing transition scholarship into dialogue with palliative care, care ethics, and relational thought, it frames phase-out as a practice of attentive accompaniment. The framework emerges from practice-informed conceptual inquiry across European and African scholarly contexts and from dialogue with hospice practitioners and circular economy scholars. A Dutch vignette explores applications to agriculture, packaging, and water management, where identity, memory, and place shape processes of change. The paper contributes to circular economy scholarship by extending care ethics to exnovation and by situating the ending of linear systems within place-based and relational transition thinking.

items.title: Repair in the Circular Economy: From Fragmented Practices to Strategic Repair Capability
items.abstract: Repair is central to the circular economy, yet research remains fragmented across product design, consumer behaviour, business models, community initiatives and policy, limiting understanding of how these dimensions interact to enable repair at scale. This study systematically reviews 79 peer‐reviewed articles using bibliometric mapping, qualitative content analysis and actor‐network analysis. Three interconnected knowledge domains emerge: user and community practices; product design, manufacturing and business models; and policy and governance. Findings show that repair outcomes depend on the alignment of organisational capabilities, ecosystem actors, infrastructure and institutional conditions, while several potentially important actors remain underexplored. Integrating these findings, we conceptualise repair as an ecosystem‐dependent strategic capability for value retention and develop a framework explaining its enabling conditions and interdependencies. The study highlights implications for firms seeking to integrate repair into circular strategies and for policymakers designing supportive repair systems, while identifying research priorities on capability development, ecosystem governance, policy effectiveness and inclusive repair systems.

items.title: Circular economy approaches for textile industry wastewater and sludge: Sustainable valorization and resource recovery
A Design-Oriented Typology of Product Take-Back Systems for Circular Value Retention
items.abstract: Background Product take-back systems are central to circular economy implementation, yet many recoverable products and materials still end up landfilled or downgraded to low-value treatment. This loss reflects misalignment among product and service design, recovery pathway structure, and the behavioral conditions that shape consumer returns. Objectives Reverse logistics, circular strategy, and behavioral research have examined these dimensions independently. However, integrated design-oriented approaches linking value retention, participation conditions, and recovery feasibility remain limited. This study examines how design decisions shape intake quality and recovery outcomes in product take-back systems. Methods A structured search initially identified 127peer-reviewed records and 48 complementary practice-based sources. Following duplicate removal, screening, and eligibility assessment, 118 sources were included in the final analytical dataset, comprising 92 peer-reviewed publications and 26 practice-based cases. Cases were coded using six analytical criteria capturing operational, behavioral, and recovery conditions. The analysis integrates R-strategy hierarchies, Capability Opportunity Motivation Behaviour (COM-B) participation conditions, and Design-for-X (DfX) principles. Results Cross-case synthesis identified eight recurring take-back strategies. These were consolidated into five higher-order solution clusters: Direct Product Reuse, Functional Restoration, Industrial Re manufacturing, Component and Material Recovery, and Risk Mitigation. Higher-value pathways were associated with design features and return-system configurations that preserved product integrity, reduced contamination, and lowered behavioral friction at the point of return. Conclusions The resulting interpretive approach links value-retention strategies with operational, behavioral, and design conditions. items.title: Beyond waste management: high-leverage transition pathways for circular construction across the building lifecycle in the UAE
items.abstract: Purpose Despite ambitious national circular economy (CE) and net-zero commitments, CE implementation in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) construction sector remains fragmented and predominantly compliance-driven, with practice largely centered on construction and demolition waste management rather than lifecycle value retention. This study investigates the implementation determinants that shape circular construction across the building lifecycle and identifies high-leverage governance interventions capable of translating policy ambition into lifecycle-integrated project delivery. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods design was employed. A systematic literature review developed a preliminary implementation determinant framework, which were subsequently refined and contextualized through semi-structured interviews with 20 UAE construction experts. The validated determinants were prioritized using integrated best–worst method (BWM) and fuzzy TOPSIS to identify the governance interventions offering the greatest leverage for lifecycle-integrated circular construction. Findings The findings indicate that although circularity is increasingly recognized across the UAE building lifecycle, implementation remains concentrated on downstream waste management and recycling, with higher-value circular strategies rarely sustained beyond the design stage. The integrated prioritization identifies regulatory coherence and financial de-risking as the principal governance levers, supported by contractual embedding, early stakeholder engagement and digital traceability. Collectively, these interventions form a sequence of high-leverage transition pathways that strengthen lifecycle continuity and improve material value retention. items.title: Enabling a Circular Economy through a Digital Product Passport in the Automotive Industry: Essential Data Points for Enhancing R-Strategies
items.abstract: The transition towards a circular economy in the manufacturing industry requires transparent and interoperable data flows across product lifecycles. Digital product passports have emerged as a key instrument to enable such transparency by providing standardized information on product composition, use, and end-of-life management. However, there is limited understanding of which specific data points are essential to operationalize such a new system and enable circular strategies within the automotive sector. This study examines how digital product passports can facilitate circular economy practices, with a focus on the car body as a representative component group. The research aims to identify and validate essential data points needed by suppliers, OEMs, and end-of-life actors to successfully use the passport and implement R-strategies effectively. A semi-systematic literature review was conducted to develop an initial data point framework, which was subsequently validated through expert interviews with stakeholders across the automotive value chain to identify potential gaps between theory and practice. The findings suggest that data points on material composition are most critical for enhancing traceability and closing material loops. At the same time, information regarding maintenance and performance is less important in the context of a car body. Moreover, the study emphasizes that pragmatic, stepwise implementation approaches are essential to ensure acceptance and feasibility across actor groups. By integrating perspectives from circular economy theory and current digital product initiatives, the study contributes an analytical framework for prioritizing data categories relevant to digital product passport development. The results can support policymakers and industry actors in aligning data requirements with circularity objectives, providing a foundation for future empirical validation.

items.title: A FERMATEAN FUZZY DEMATEL–ISM FRAMEWORK FOR LIFE-CYCLE INTELLIGENCE AND CIRCULAR VALUE RETENTION IN THE PLYWOOD INDUSTRY
items.abstract: The plywood industry is traditionally organized around linear production and consumption pathways in which engineered wood products progress from raw-material conversion to manufacturing, utilization, and eventual disposal. The difficulties of product traceability, embedded material separability, recovery of the adhesive and embedded materials, re-using them and end-of-life management are new challenges that arise, particularly regarding the amount of embedded material value that cannot be recovered with this linear structure. In this study, a new definition of life-cycle intelligence for circular value retention in the plywood industry is put forward, where the continuous optimization of production is transitioning into the ability to maintain material functionality and recoverability across multiple product life cycles. The developed hybrid Fermatean Fuzzy Decision-Making Trial and Evaluation Laboratory (FF-DMTEL) and Interpretive Structural Modelling (ISM) is used for investigation on the causal structure of Critical life cycle enablers. The framework also includes new concepts such as passports for plywood material, digital product traceability, reversible joining solutions, recoverability of adhesives, design-for-disassembly approach, valorizing residual panels, cascading reuse approach, remanufacturing pathways, component-level grading, the logistics of recovery, artificial intelligence for material identification and Lifecycle Carbon tracking and secondary markets integration. The interdependencies between obvious stakeholders in the plywood supply chain, under uncertainty, are modeled through the expert assessments of plywood manufacturers, material specialists, recovery specialists, and professionals. The enablers and their temporal interconnectedness and turning paths are identified by ISM, and the causal influences and prominence are found by DEMATEL. items.title: The Lean-Circular Transition in Morocco: Evidence from the Manufacturing and Construction Sectors
items.venue: International Journal of Strategic Management and Economic Studies (IJSMES)
items.abstract: The depletion of natural resources and growing environmental pressure have prompted interest in linking Lean management and the circular economy as complementary approaches to sustainable industrial transformation. This article offers a narrative review of the literature on how both paradigms interact, with particular attention to the Moroccan context, an angle still scarcely explored in the specialised literature. It examines the synergy mechanisms, enabling conditions, barriers and performance outcomes documented in recent studies on Moroccan manufacturing and construction SMEs. The review shows that Lean tools such as value stream mapping and 5S frequently serve as operational foundations for implementing circular economy principles. Persistent tensions are also identified, among them the risk of a narrow interpretation of Lean, which may constrain the systemic thinking that genuine circularity requires. The Moroccan evidence reveals that small and medium-sized enterprises increasingly draw on Circular Lean Six Sigma 4.0 and Lean Construction practices, although institutional barriers, particularly around public procurement governance, continue to constrain their translation into sustained circular outcomes. The synergy between Lean and the circular economy holds considerable potential, whose realisation requires rethinking Lean from a broader value-retention perspective, adapted to Morocco's institutional conditions.

items.title: CoSphere-SLAM: Multi-Agent Panoramic Gaussian Splatting SLAM with Spherical Loop Closure
items.abstract: Dense collaborative mapping is essential for search and rescue, building inspection, and warehouse automation, where panoramic cameras capture the entire surroundings in a single frame. Unlike pinhole agents that share views only at similar headings, panoramic agents observe overlapping scenes at any 3D orientation, yet searching full rotations also produces mutually consistent false loop closures across distinct symmetric rooms. Moreover, continuous monocular scale drift splits rigidly merged maps at revisited surfaces, while depth noise at short baselines distorts loop translation directions. To address these challenges, we propose CoSphere-SLAM, the first multi-agent Gaussian splatting SLAM framework for panoramic cameras, whose spherical loop closure aligns spherical features over $\mathrm{SO}(3)$ via fast Fourier correlation across arbitrary orientations and rejects symmetric false closures through global $\mathrm{Sim}(3)$ consensus. Building on these closures, directional global optimization solves a per-keyframe $\mathrm{Sim}(3)$ pose graph with log-scale regularization to correct scale drift while separating optical-flow translation directions from depth-based magnitudes. Finally, omnidirectional Gaussian fusion transforms each Gaussian with its keyframe similarity and renders Gaussians at their maximum ray response to jointly refine poses and maps. Experiments on indoor and cross-session multi-agent panoramic benchmarks demonstrate that CoSphere-SLAM achieves state-of-the-art trajectory accuracy and rendering quality among single-agent and multi-agent methods. Project website: https://cosphere-slam.github.io.

items.title: Embedding Circularity in Conceptual Building Design: A Functional Framework for Data-Driven Decisions during the Earliest Architectural Design Stages
items.venue: SpringerBriefs in applied sciences and technology
items.abstract: Circularity in the built environment is ultimately a design governance challenge rather than a purely technical one. While methodological support is increasingly available, its effectiveness depends on the capacity of project stakeholders to align early-stage decisions with long-term value retention, data continuity, and recovery infrastructures. In this context, the transition toward circular building design requires not only improved tools, but also institutional integration across design, procurement, and regulatory systems, enabling circular criteria to become embedded as standard design constraints rather than optional sustainability objectives. The coming convergence of digitalization, such as BIM and digital product passports, together with lifecycle regulation, and performance-based assessment frameworks will likely redefine the role of the conceptual design phase as a decision environment where circularity is operationalized, verified, and governed from the outset. Consequently, the advancement of circular architecture will depend less on the development of new isolated instruments and more on the systematic integration of existing knowledge into coherent, enforceable, and practice-oriented design processes, capable of bridging the gap between circular economy ambition and built reality.

items.title: Survivalist circularity: theorising fragility and displacement within necessity-driven circular economies
items.abstract: The scholarship on circular economy (CE) is increasingly recognising that in low income contexts, repair, reuse, repurposing, second-hand exchange and material recovery may be driven by economic necessity rather than environmental intention. This paper builds on the established necessity-driven circular economy and develops a narrower, mechanism-level construct of survivalist circularity. Survivalist circularity is defined as circular material practices that can only be sustained under a binding material or livelihood constraint. The construct and its boundaries are defined by a purposive conceptual synthesis of CE, informal recovery, sustainable-livelihoods, frugal-innovation, value-retention, measurement and just-transition literatures. Five testable propositions and a two-axis model relate material constraint to institutional support for value retention. The main prediction is conditional displacement, whereby relaxing a binding constraint decreases the necessity-attributable component of circular practice, while total circularity decreases only where designed, institutional, market or value-based drivers do not substitute. Our paper makes four contributions. It theoretically detects a constraint-contingent mechanism and a temporal displacement risk in necessity-driven CE. It distinguishes survivalist circularity from informality, frugal innovation and geographic or poverty labels in terms of construction. Methodologically, it prioritises the distinction between formal CE institutionalisation and directly observed material practice. In policy, it defines institutional substitution as the sequencing of repair access, secondary markets, safe recovery systems and worker protections before or as necessity weakens. Thus the construct is not a label for Global South or low-income circularity generally, but a testable causal regime, whose value for empirical work depends on demonstrating counterfactual dependence on constraint.

items.title: Circular potential of insulating glass units—a sensitivity study on life cycle impact assessment
items.abstract: Creating closed material loops through value-retention processes is essential for circular economy (CE) strategies in construction, particularly for energy-intensive materials such as glass in insulating glass units (IGUs). In practice, IGUs are often demolished with a façade and treated as mixed construction-and-demolition waste, causing material dissipation and avoidable environmental burdens. Although circular approaches for IGUs are emerging, comparative life cycle impact assessments (LCIA) across realistic system boundaries and disassembly practices remain scarce due to construction diversity, limited data availability, and uncertainties in disassembly processes. This study addresses this gap by providing reproducible LCIAs of promising IGU end-of-life (EoL) scenarios based on ecoinvent data and literature. Prospective scenarios for treating obsolete IGUs and processing components into triple IGUs resemble a “grave-to-gate” phase beyond an IGU’s first life. This phase incorporates sequences of disassembly, quality assessment, transport and secondary manufacturing to quantify the Global Warming Potential of the scenarios in kg CO 2 -equivalent per square meter of triple IGU. Modelling approaches include best practice assumptions and scenario-based material flows. Results show promising potential for reducing the impact of triple IGUs through remanufacturing. Sensitivity analyses were conducted for transport and process parameters. The results show that the acceptance rate during qualification is the most important parameter for sustainable pathways. The transport analysis indicates that qualification and disassembly should be located close to the dismantling process where possible. This study’s results contribute to data-driven selection of sustainable pathways and to understanding the relevance of future research topics in circularity of architectural glass.

items.title: Diagnosing Operational Waste and Barriers to Material-Value Retention in Project-Based Welding: An Integrated VSM-PAM and Thematic Analysis Approach
items.abstract: Project-based welding combines variable work content, parallel component flows, and interdependent quality-control activities, making it difficult to diagnose operational waste and barriers to material-value retention simultaneously. This exploratory single-case study applied an integrated current-state framework combining Value Stream Mapping (VSM), Process Activity Mapping (PAM), eight-waste identification, and NVivo-assisted thematic analysis to a rolling-stock welding value stream. Data were collected through direct observation, a gemba walk, and semi-structured interviews with four production and quality-control personnel. The current-state VSM recorded a total lead time of 609,358 s (169.27 h), comprising 324,867 s (90.24 h) of processing and 284,491 s (79.03 h) of waiting. PAM provisionally classified 53.21% of lead time as value-adding, 0.10% as necessary non-value-adding, and 46.69% as non-value-adding waiting. All eight lean wastes were identified. Thematic analysis generated 138 coding references across ten subthemes and five principal themes. The most prominent factors concerned welding-standard and sequence compliance, inspection and quality control, resource readiness, coordination and information exchange, and operator competence and discipline. Circularity-related evidence emerged from scrap segregation, potential reuse of residual materials, and efficient use of production resources. The integrated findings indicate that waiting, work-in-process accumulation, over-welding, defects, and rework arise from interconnected process, quality, resource-readiness, human, and organizational conditions. The study presents an integrated qualitative diagnosis that links operational waste to barriers to retaining material value in project-based welding.

items.title: From Conflict to Continuity: Circular Strategies for Transformative Urban Renewal
items.abstract: Urban renewal in contemporary Europe must address overlapping crises -climate change, social fragmentation, and economic precarity -while overcoming the limits of past linear planning models.Current approaches, such as temporary or adaptive reuse, often fail to ensure long-term impact, privileging short-term outputs.Circularity is expanded beyond ecological goals to include spatial, social, and temporal dimensions.It is understood not only as closing material loops but as fostering durable relationships among stakeholders, governance levels, and evolving uses of space.The article argues that urban renewal becomes transformative only when conceived as an ongoing and circular regenerative process rather than a finite intervention, raising the question: what conflicts shape current renewal practices?The analysis draws on qualitative case studies across European cities and towns (including Palermo, Madrid, Leipzig, Hannover, Celle, and San Vito dei Normanni) and is based on fieldwork, interviews, and document analysis.A comparative reading identifies five recurring conflict types -economic, social, cultural, political, and managerial, often persisting beyond project completion.Findings reveal that linear models tend to generate or amplify conflicts when interventions neglect local values, lack institutional continuity, or fail to address long-term management.In response, the article proposes three pillars: socially innovative co-production, circular regeneration integrating memory and transformation, and governance loops ensuring continuity and adaptability.Ultimately, the study reframes urban renewal as an open-ended, regenerative process where conflict becomes a resource, supporting more inclusive and resilient urban transformations.

items.title: Climate Land Trust: Designing Relational Pathways for Circular Urban Transformation
items.abstract: Contemporary circular urban development often prioritises material cycles and technical efficiency while overlooking questions of land ownership, care, and long-term responsibility.This article advances circular urbanism beyond technical and materialist approaches towards relational, ecological, and social forms of circularity.It introduces the Climate Land Trust as a conceptual design framework for regenerative urban transformation, grounded in relational land-use practices.Building on community land trusts and commons-based models, it positions land as a non-commodified good, incorporating ecological stewardship and fostering community-led and more-than-human care.Circularity encompasses dynamic social and ecological cycles, including the reuse of land and materials and the regeneration of soil, water, and community through mutual care and knowledge exchange.Drawing on a case study in Barcelona, the article discusses the framework's potential climate adaptability at broader urban scales
cites_core: The Metabolism of Cities

items.title: SYSTEMATISATION OF METHODOLOGICAL APPROACHES AND METHODS FOR ASSESSING CIRCULARITY IN THE NATIONAL ECONOMY
items.abstract: This article systematises methodological approaches to the comprehensive assessment of circularity in the national economy. It substantiates a seven-dimensional conceptual framework that combines material flows, resource efficiency, circular material use, life-cycle impacts, value retention, economic and econometric assessment, and institutional and integrated evaluation. The complementary roles of material flow analysis (MFA), economy-wide material flow accounts (EW-MFA), domestic material consumption (DMC), raw material consumption (RMC), circular material use rate (CMU), life cycle assessment (LCA), input–output and environmentally extended input–output analysis (IO/EEIO), and key performance indicators (KPIs) are clarified. Particular attention is paid to double counting, statistical coverage, system boundaries, and causal interpretation. The findings are conceptual and methodological; empirical validation using national statistics remains a task for subsequent research.

items.title: Developments in chemical depolymerization techniques for circular recycling of polyesters: Emphasis on hydrolysis, methanolysis, and ethanolysis
items.abstract: Chemical depolymerization is emerging as a key enabler of polymer circularity as demand grows for sustainable resource use and improved management of synthetic waste. Unlike mechanical recycling, which often yields downcycled materials, depolymerization cleaves polymer chains to recover high-purity monomers and intermediates suitable for re-polymerization or upgrading into value-added chemicals. This review provides a critical, cross-route assessment of three major PET depolymerization pathways Hydrolysis, Methanolysis, and Ethanolysis highlighting reaction mechanisms, catalyst development, and process conditions. Hydrolysis, especially in hot-compressed water (HCW), tolerates mixed and contaminated feedstocks and can reduce pretreatment demands, but it remains energy intensive and faces corrosion, salt formation, and challenging aqueous separations. Methanolysis is advancing toward industrial deployment: pilot and demonstration efforts report high dimethyl terephthalate (DMT) yields and high-purity ethylene glycol (EG), while defect-engineered catalysts and bio-based co-solvents increasingly improve rates and lower environmental burden. Ethanolysis is less mature but can leverage bioethanol supply chains and enables selective depolymerization of polyester/cotton blends; however, slower kinetics and more complex separations limit productivity. Beyond chemistry, we discuss reactor innovations, process intensification, integrated flowsheets, solvent-loop closure, and control strategies relevant to scale-up. Remaining barriers include catalyst toxicity, solvent recovery and purification costs, feedstock variability, and overall techno-economic feasibility.

items.title: Enhancing circular textile waste recycling: a comparative analysis of European countries and South Korea
items.abstract: The rapid increase in textile waste has intensified the need for effective strategies to establish circular textile management systems. This study evaluates textile waste management policies in South Korea through a comparative analysis with selected European countries and examines multiple recycling pathways, including mechanical recycling, chemical recycling, and energy recovery. The comparative policy analysis showed that the European countries generally covered a broader range of life-cycle stages and included economic and communication instruments that were not identified in South Korea. Product quality analysis further confirmed that qualified recycled products can be obtained through selected recycling pathways, indicating the technical applicability of textile waste recycling. However, policy and technological improvements are still required to support practical implementation. To address these challenges, this study proposes integrated policy and technology measures, including textile extended producer responsibility (EPR), recyclable design, digital product passport (DPP)-based tracking, advanced sorting, recycled-content requirements, and financial incentives. A hierarchical prioritization framework based on material circularity, value retention, and environmental considerations is also suggested to support the development of circular textile management systems.

Molten-Salt Etching for Silicon Photovoltaic Recycling: A Pathway from Downcycling to Wafer Upcycling and Circular Manufacturing

items.title: A Break-Even Threshold Framework for Circular Digital Transitions on Family Farms: Precision Agriculture and Blockchain Traceability in Rural Colombia
items.abstract: Digital technologies are promoted as enablers of circular agri-food systems, yet family farms lack tools to judge whether such investments pay off, and economic data at this scale are often unreliable. This study develops a break-even threshold framework that evaluates digital investments using only physical and price variables, derives three propositions on entry costs, decision robustness and unreliable data, and applies it to precision agriculture with blockchain traceability on 100 family farms in Sumapaz, Bogotá, Colombia, 50 of them adopters. Three circular dimensions were assessed: the narrowing of resource flows, value retention and chain governance. Adopting farms used 26 to 42% fewer inputs per tonne of output and recorded fewer batch rejections and intermediaries. The investment broke even with a yield gain of 2.51% against an observed differential of 19.95%, and all farms remained viable if only half of that differential were retained, if half of the additional output went unsold or if technology costs doubled. Viability depended on the ratio of investment to farm area, with an elasticity of −0.65, and no price premium for verified origin was found. The framework turns transition narratives into a computable decision rule and identifies entry cost as the main barrier for smallholders.

items.abstract: The article examined production chain management based on circular economy principles, focusing on the building materials industry. Systems thinking, comparative analysis, synthesis and statistical data analysis were applied. Joint planning of forward and reverse resource flows, secondary material use and stakeholder coordination were examined. A circularity coefficient and a composite coordination indicator were proposed. Resource value retention strategies were assigned to production stages. A conceptual model integrated forward flows, reverse loops and management processes. Recommendations addressed contractual arrangements, digital tracking and secondary material quality. The findings provided a theoretical and methodological basis for improving resource efficiency and organising return flows within production chains.
